AND

2.2 Delayed payment shall carry interest @ l2% per annum.

9.1 The Service Provider shall indemnify the Client against third party claims of IP infringement

# PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT

**Crestline Contract No.:** CRI-VND-24-0318
**Effective Date:** August 1, 2024

This Professional Services Agreement (this "**Agreement**") is entered into as of the Effective Date by and between:

**CRESTLINE RETAIL INC.**, an Ohio corporation with its principal place of business at 250 West Nationwide Boulevard, Suite 900, Columbus, Ohio 43215 ("**Crestline**"); and

**ATLIQ INC.**, a Delaware corporation (EIN 88-4410273) with its office at 101 College Road East, Suite 210, Princeton, New Jersey 08540 ("**Supplier**").

Crestline and Supplier are each a "**Party**" and collectively the "**Parties**."

## RECITALS

WHEREAS, Crestline operates retail stores and e-commerce channels in the United States and requires data engineering and business intelligence resources on a time-and-materials basis; and

WHEREAS, Supplier is in the business of providing such resources and wishes to provide them to Crestline on the terms set out below.

NOW, THEREFORE, for good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are acknowledged, the Parties agree as follows:

## 1. DEFINITIONS

1.1 "**Affiliate**" means any entity that directly or indirectly controls, is controlled by, or is under common control with a Party, where "control" means ownership of more than fifty percent (50%) of the voting interests of the entity or the power to direct its management.

1.2 "**Confidential Information**" means all non-public information disclosed by a Party that is designated as confidential or that a reasonable person would understand to be confidential.

1.3 "**Deliverables**" means all work product created by Supplier Personnel specifically for Crestline under a Work Order.

1.4 "**Rate Card**" means the hourly rates set out in Exhibit B.

1.5 "**Supplier Personnel**" means employees and approved subcontractors of Supplier assigned to perform Services.

1.6 "**Work Order**" means an order for Services substantially in the form of Exhibit A, executed by both Parties.

## 2. SERVICES

2.1 Supplier shall provide the data engineering, business intelligence and analytics services described in each Work Order (the "**Services**").

2.2 Each Work Order shall specify the roles, estimated hours, duration, and any Deliverables. Each Work Order is governed by this Agreement.

2.3 Crestline's primary contact for this Agreement is Laura Brennan, VP Data.

## 3. SUPPLIER PERSONNEL

3.1 Supplier shall assign qualified Supplier Personnel with skills commensurate with the roles in the Rate Card. Crestline may request the replacement of any Supplier Personnel on reasonable grounds on ten (10) business days' notice.

3.2 Supplier Personnel shall comply with Crestline's information security, acceptable use and on-site policies.

3.3 Supplier is an independent contractor and is solely responsible for the compensation, benefits and taxes of Supplier Personnel.

## 4. TERM

4.1 This Agreement commences on the Effective Date and continues for three (3) years, until July 31, 2027, unless earlier terminated under Section 11.

4.2 Work Orders in effect at expiry shall continue to be governed by this Agreement until completed or terminated.

## 5. TIMEKEEPING AND INVOICING

5.1 Supplier Personnel shall record time in Crestline's designated timekeeping system, and time shall be approved weekly by the Crestline Work Order manager.

5.2 Supplier shall invoice monthly in arrears for approved hours at the applicable Rate Card rates.

5.3 Crestline shall pay undisputed invoices within thirty (30) days of receipt.

5.4 Travel expenses are reimbursable only if pre-approved in writing and incurred in accordance with Crestline's travel policy.

## 6. RATES

6.1 The rates for Services are set out in the Rate Card (Exhibit B).

6.2 The Rate Card rates are fixed for the first twelve (12) months of the Term. Thereafter, Supplier may increase rates once per contract year by no more than three percent (3%) upon sixty (60) days' prior written notice.

6.3 Rates are inclusive of all Supplier overheads, equipment and administrative costs.

6.4 Supplier represents and warrants that the rates, fees and other commercial terms offered to Crestline under this Agreement are and shall remain no less favorable than those offered by Supplier or its Affiliates to any other customer for substantially similar services during the Term. If, during the Term, Supplier or any of its Affiliates offers lower rates to any other customer for substantially similar services, Supplier shall promptly notify Crestline, and such lower rates shall apply to Crestline retroactively from the date they were first offered to such other customer. Supplier shall issue a credit to Crestline for the difference between the amounts invoiced and the amounts that would have been invoiced at such lower rates, within thirty (30) days.

6.5 Upon reasonable notice and no more than once per year, Crestline or an independent auditor bound by confidentiality may audit Supplier's records to verify compliance with this Section 6.

## 7. CONFIDENTIALITY

7.1 Each Party shall hold the other Party's Confidential Information in confidence, use it only to perform or receive the Services, and disclose it only to its personnel and advisors with a need to know who are bound by obligations at least as protective.

7.2 The obligations in Section 7.1 do not apply to information that is or becomes publicly available without breach, was known to the recipient prior to disclosure, is independently developed, or is rightfully received from a third party.

7.3 These obligations survive for three (3) years following termination, and indefinitely for trade secrets.

## 8. INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY

8.1 Upon payment, Crestline shall own all right, title and interest in the Deliverables.

8.2 Supplier retains all rights in its pre-existing materials, tools and know-how ("**Supplier Materials**"). To the extent Supplier Materials are incorporated in a Deliverable, Supplier grants Crestline a non-exclusive, perpetual, royalty-free license to use them as part of such Deliverable.

## 9. WARRANTIES

9.1 Supplier warrants that the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with generally accepted industry standards.

9.2 EXCEPT AS EXPRESSLY SET FORTH IN THIS AGREEMENT, NEITHER PARTY MAKES ANY OTHER WARRANTY, EXPRESS OR IMPLIED, INCLUDING ANY WARRANTY OF MERCHANTABILITY OR FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE.

## 10. INDEMNIFICATION

10.1 Supplier shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Crestline from third-party claims arising from (a) Supplier's gross negligence or willful misconduct, (b) infringement by the Deliverables of any third-party intellectual property right, or (c) any claim by Supplier Personnel for wages, benefits or employment status.

10.2 Crestline shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Supplier from third-party claims arising from materials provided by Crestline or Crestline's gross negligence or willful misconduct.

## 11. TERMINATION

11.1 Either Party may terminate this Agreement or any Work Order for convenience on thirty (30) days' written notice.

11.2 Either Party may terminate this Agreement upon written notice if the other Party materially breaches it and fails to cure within thirty (30) days.

11.3 Upon termination, Crestline shall pay for all approved hours performed through the effective date of termination.

## 12. LIMITATION OF LIABILITY

12.1 EXCEPT FOR BREACH OF SECTION 7 OR A PARTY'S INDEMNIFICATION OBLIGATIONS, NEITHER PARTY SHALL BE LIABLE FOR ANY INDIRECT, INCIDENTAL, CONSEQUENTIAL, SPECIAL OR PUNITIVE DAMAGES.

12.2 EXCEPT FOR BREACH OF SECTION 7 OR A PARTY'S INDEMNIFICATION OBLIGATIONS, EACH PARTY'S AGGREGATE LIABILITY SHALL NOT EXCEED THE FEES PAID OR PAYABLE BY CRESTLINE UNDER THIS AGREEMENT IN THE TWELVE (12) MONTHS PRECEDING THE CLAIM.

## 13. DATA SECURITY

13.1 Supplier shall comply with Crestline's Vendor Data Security Requirements, as updated from time to time, and all applicable U.S. federal and state privacy laws, including the Ohio Data Protection Act where applicable.

13.2 Supplier shall notify Crestline within seventy-two (72) hours of becoming aware of any security incident affecting Crestline data.

13.3 Supplier shall not access Crestline production data from outside the United States without Crestline's prior written approval.

## 14. INSURANCE

14.1 Supplier shall maintain commercial general liability insurance of at least $1,000,000 per occurrence, professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of at least $2,000,000, and workers' compensation insurance as required by law.

## 15. NON-SOLICITATION

15.1 During the Term and for twelve (12) months thereafter, Crestline shall not directly solicit for employment any Supplier Personnel assigned to Crestline, save with Supplier's consent.

## 16. GOVERNING LAW; VENUE

16.1 This Agreement shall be governed by the laws of the State of Ohio, without regard to its conflict-of-laws principles.

16.2 The Parties consent to the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts located in Franklin County, Ohio.

## 17. MISCELLANEOUS

17.1 Neither Party may assign this Agreement without the other Party's prior written consent, except to a successor in a merger or sale of substantially all assets.

17.2 This Agreement, including its Exhibits and Work Orders, is the entire agreement between the Parties and supersedes all prior agreements relating to its subject matter.

17.3 Any amendment must be in writing and signed by both Parties. Waiver of any breach is not a waiver of any other breach.

17.4 Notices shall be sent to: Crestline — Attn: VP Data, with copy to Legal Department, at the address above; Supplier — Attn: President, at the address above, with a copy to karandeep@atliq.com.

17.5 This Agreement may be signed in counterparts and electronically.

# MUTUAL NON-DISCLOSURE AGREEMENT

**Date:** 22 January 2025

## PARTIES

This Mutual Non-Disclosure Agreement (the "**Agreement**") is made between:

1. **AL NOOR HOSPITALITY GROUP LLC**, a limited liability company registered in the Emirate of Dubai, United Arab Emirates, having its principal office at Level 22, Al Noor Tower, Sheikh Zayed Road, PO Box 118834, Dubai, United Arab Emirates ("**Al Noor**"); and

2. **ATLIQ TECHNOLOGIES PRIVATE LIMITED**, a private limited company incorporated under the laws of India (CIN U72900MH2019PTC321456; GSTIN 27AAKCA4821F1Z3), having its registered office at 4th Floor, Baner Business Bay, Pune 411045, Maharashtra, India ("**AtliQ**"),

each a "**Party**" and together the "**Parties**".

## RECITALS

A. The Parties are discussing a possible engagement under which AtliQ would design and implement a guest analytics platform for Al Noor's hotel portfolio (the "**Purpose**").

B. In the course of those discussions each Party expects to disclose to the other certain confidential information, and each Party wishes to protect its information on equal terms.

## 1. DEFINITIONS

1.1 "**Confidential Information**" means any information disclosed by one Party (the "**Disclosing Party**") to the other Party (the "**Receiving Party**") in connection with the Purpose, whether before or after the date of this Agreement, in any form, that is marked or identified as confidential or that a reasonable person would understand to be confidential, including guest and occupancy data, pricing, commercial proposals, solution architecture, source code, methodologies and business plans.

1.2 "**Representatives**" means a Party's directors, officers, employees, professional advisers and subcontractors who need to know the Confidential Information for the Purpose.

## 2. OBLIGATIONS OF THE RECEIVING PARTY

2.1 Each Party, as Receiving Party, shall:
   (a) use the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information solely for the Purpose;
   (b) not disclose it to any third party other than its Representatives who are bound by confidentiality obligations no less protective than those in this Agreement;
   (c) protect it using at least the same degree of care it uses for its own confidential information, and no less than reasonable care; and
   (d) promptly notify the Disclosing Party on becoming aware of any unauthorised use or disclosure.

2.2 Each Party is responsible for any breach of this Agreement by its Representatives.

## 3. EXCLUSIONS

3.1 The obligations in Clause 2 do not apply to information that the Receiving Party can demonstrate:
   (a) is or becomes publicly available other than through a breach of this Agreement;
   (b) was lawfully in its possession before disclosure by the Disclosing Party;
   (c) is lawfully received from a third party without a duty of confidentiality; or
   (d) is independently developed without use of or reference to the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information.

3.2 A Receiving Party may disclose Confidential Information where required by law, regulation or order of a competent court or authority, provided that (where lawful) it gives the Disclosing Party prompt prior notice and discloses only the minimum required.

## 4. PERSONAL DATA

4.1 Where Confidential Information includes personal data of guests or employees, the Receiving Party shall process it only as necessary for the Purpose and in accordance with applicable data protection law, including the UAE Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 and the Indian Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, as applicable.

## 5. RETURN AND DESTRUCTION

5.1 On written request of the Disclosing Party, or on termination of discussions, the Receiving Party shall promptly return or destroy the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information, save for copies retained in routine electronic back-ups or as required by law, which remain subject to this Agreement.

## 6. TERM

6.1 This Agreement applies to disclosures made during the period of two (2) years from its date. Either Party may end that period earlier by thirty (30) days' written notice.

6.2 The obligations in Clauses 2 to 5 shall continue for five (5) years from the date of each disclosure.

## 7. NO LICENCE; NO OBLIGATION

7.1 All Confidential Information remains the property of the Disclosing Party. No licence or other right is granted except as expressly stated.

7.2 Nothing in this Agreement obliges either Party to enter into any further agreement or transaction.

## 8. REMEDIES

8.1 Each Party acknowledges that damages may not be an adequate remedy for breach, and that the Disclosing Party may seek injunctive or equitable relief in addition to any other remedy.

## 9. GENERAL

9.1 This Agreement is the entire agreement between the Parties on its subject matter and may be amended only in writing signed by both Parties.

9.2 Neither Party may assign this Agreement without the prior written consent of the other.

9.3 This Agreement is governed by the laws of India. Any dispute shall be referred to arbitration by a sole arbitrator under the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, seated in Mumbai, conducted in English.

9.4 This Agreement may be executed in counterparts and by electronic signature.

# MASTER SERVICES AGREEMENT

**PayTrack Ref:** PT/LEGAL/MSA/2025/004
**Execution Version — 22 January 2025**

This Master Services Agreement ("**Agreement**") is entered into on 22 January 2025 ("**Effective Date**") between:

**PAYTRACK TECHNOLOGIES PRIVATE LIMITED**, a company incorporated under the Companies Act, 2013, having its registered office at 3rd Floor, Prestige Tech Vista, Outer Ring Road, Bellandur, Bengaluru 560103, Karnataka, India ("**PayTrack**" or "**Client**"); and

**ATLIQ TECHNOLOGIES PRIVATE LIMITED**, a company incorporated under the Companies Act, 2013 (CIN U72900MH2019PTC321456; GSTIN 27AAKCA4821F1Z3), having its registered office at 4th Floor, Baner Business Bay, Pune 411045, Maharashtra, India ("**AtliQ**" or "**Vendor**").

## RECITALS

A. PayTrack operates a payments reconciliation and merchant settlement platform and wishes to build a transaction analytics and anomaly detection module.

B. AtliQ provides data engineering, machine learning and software development services.

C. The Parties wish to set out the terms on which AtliQ will provide such services.

## 1. DEFINITIONS

1.1 "**Applicable Law**" means all laws, regulations, and binding directions of any governmental or regulatory authority, including the Reserve Bank of India, applicable to a Party.

1.2 "**Client Data**" means all data, including transaction data and merchant data, provided by or on behalf of PayTrack.

1.3 "**Deliverables**" means all software, models, code, documentation and other materials delivered under an SOW.

1.4 "**Losses**" means all losses, damages, liabilities, costs (including reasonable legal fees), fines and penalties.

1.5 "**SOW**" means a statement of work executed by both Parties under this Agreement.

## 2. SCOPE

2.1 AtliQ shall perform the services set out in each SOW ("**Services**"). SOW-1 covers the design and development of a transaction analytics data platform and an ML-based anomaly detection module for merchant settlements.

2.2 PayTrack's relationship owner is Ms. Shreya Iyer.

2.3 AtliQ shall comply with PayTrack's information security policies and the RBI guidelines on outsourcing of IT services as communicated by PayTrack in writing.

## 3. CHANGE CONTROL

3.1 Any change to the scope, timeline or fees under an SOW shall be documented in a change order signed by both Parties.

## 4. FEES AND PAYMENT

4.1 The total fees under SOW-1 are **USD 71,000** (United States Dollars Seventy-One Thousand only), payable in accordance with the milestone schedule in SOW-1.

4.2 AtliQ shall invoice upon completion of each milestone. PayTrack shall pay each undisputed invoice within thirty (30) days of receipt.

4.3 Fees are exclusive of GST. PayTrack may deduct TDS in accordance with Applicable Law.

## 5. TERM AND TERMINATION

5.1 This Agreement shall commence on the Effective Date and continue for two (2) years unless terminated earlier.

5.2 Either Party may terminate for material breach not remedied within thirty (30) days of written notice.

5.3 PayTrack may terminate an SOW for convenience on thirty (30) days' notice, subject to payment for all Services performed and committed costs up to the termination date.

5.4 PayTrack may terminate this Agreement if directed to do so by a regulator, on such notice as the regulator requires.

## 6. ACCEPTANCE

6.1 PayTrack shall review each Deliverable within ten (10) business days. Deliverables shall be deemed accepted if no written rejection specifying material non-conformities is received within that period.

## 7. CONFIDENTIALITY

7.1 Each Party shall keep confidential the other Party's confidential information and use it only for the purposes of this Agreement.

7.2 AtliQ acknowledges that Client Data may include payment system data subject to RBI data localisation requirements, and shall ensure that such data is stored only in India.

7.3 These obligations survive for five (5) years following termination, and indefinitely in respect of Client Data.

## 8. INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY

8.1 Upon full payment, all intellectual property in the Deliverables developed specifically for PayTrack shall vest in PayTrack.

8.2 AtliQ retains ownership of its pre-existing materials, tools and know-how and grants PayTrack a perpetual, non-exclusive, royalty-free licence to use such materials as incorporated in the Deliverables.

## 9. WARRANTIES

9.1 AtliQ warrants that the Services will be performed with reasonable skill and care and in accordance with Applicable Law, and that the Deliverables will materially conform to the SOW for ninety (90) days after acceptance.

9.2 PayTrack warrants that it has the necessary rights and consents to provide Client Data to AtliQ for the purposes of the Services.

## 10. INDEMNITY

10.1 Each Party (the "**Indemnifying Party**") shall indemnify, defend and hold harmless the other Party and its directors, officers and employees (the "**Indemnified Party**") from and against all Losses arising out of any third-party claim to the extent caused by: (a) the Indemnifying Party's breach of Clause 7 (Confidentiality) or Clause 12 (Data Protection); (b) the gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud of the Indemnifying Party or its personnel; or (c) in the case of AtliQ, any claim that the Deliverables infringe a third party's intellectual property rights, and in the case of PayTrack, any claim that Client Data or materials supplied by PayTrack infringe a third party's rights.

10.2 Neither Party shall be required to indemnify the other to the extent any Losses are caused by the negligence, breach or wilful misconduct of the Indemnified Party.

10.3 The Indemnified Party shall give prompt written notice of any claim, permit the Indemnifying Party to control the defence and settlement, and provide reasonable cooperation at the Indemnifying Party's cost.

## 11. LIMITATION OF LIABILITY

11.1 Neither Party shall be liable for any indirect, special, incidental or consequential damages, or loss of profits, revenue or goodwill.

11.2 Each Party's total aggregate liability under or in connection with this Agreement shall not exceed the total fees paid or payable under the SOW giving rise to the claim.

11.3 The limitations in this Clause 11 shall not apply to liability for fraud or wilful misconduct.

## 12. DATA PROTECTION

12.1 AtliQ shall process personal data comprised in Client Data only on PayTrack's documented instructions and in compliance with the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, the Information Technology Act, 2000 and applicable RBI directions.

12.2 AtliQ shall notify PayTrack of any data breach within twenty-four (24) hours of becoming aware of it, and shall cooperate with PayTrack in any reporting to CERT-In or the RBI.

12.3 AtliQ shall permit PayTrack and its regulators to audit its compliance with this Clause 12 on reasonable notice.

## 13. NON-SOLICITATION

13.1 Neither Party shall solicit for employment the other Party's employees engaged in the Services during the term and for twelve (12) months thereafter.

## 14. FORCE MAJEURE

14.1 Neither Party shall be liable for delay or non-performance caused by events beyond its reasonable control. AtliQ shall maintain a business continuity plan appropriate to the Services.

## 15. GOVERNING LAW AND DISPUTE RESOLUTION

15.1 This Agreement shall be governed by the laws of India.

15.2 Disputes not resolved by negotiation between senior management within thirty (30) days shall be referred to arbitration by a sole arbitrator under the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996. The seat and venue of arbitration shall be Pune, and the language shall be English.

## 16. GENERAL

16.1 Neither Party may assign this Agreement without the prior written consent of the other.

16.2 This Agreement, with its SOWs, constitutes the entire agreement between the Parties and supersedes all prior drafts and negotiations.

16.3 Amendments must be in writing and signed by authorised representatives of both Parties.

16.4 This Agreement may be executed electronically and in counterparts.

# MASTER SERVICES AGREEMENT

This Master Services Agreement ("**Agreement**") is executed at Chennai on this 10th day of March 2025 ("**Effective Date**")

**BY AND BETWEEN**

**ACME RETAIL GROUP PRIVATE LIMITED**, a company incorporated under the Companies Act, 2013, having its registered office at No. 45, Anna Salai, Teynampet, Chennai 600018, Tamil Nadu, India (hereinafter referred to as the "**Client**", which expression shall, unless repugnant to the context, include its successors and permitted assigns) of the ONE PART;

**AND**

**ATLIQ TECHNOLOGIES PRIVATE LIMITED**, a company incorporated under the Companies Act, 2013 (CIN U72900MH2019PTC321456; GSTIN 27AAKCA4821F1Z3), having its registered office at 4th Floor, Baner Business Bay, Pune 411045, Maharashtra, India (hereinafter referred to as the "**Service Provider**", which expression shall, unless repugnant to the context, include its successors and permitted assigns) of the OTHER PART.

## RECITALS

WHEREAS the Client operates a chain of retail stores in South India and wishes to implement enterprise Power BI dashboards for sales, inventory and store performance reporting;

WHEREAS the Service Provider is engaged in the business of software development, data analytics and business intelligence services; and

WHEREAS the Parties wish to record the terms on which the Service Provider will render such services.

NOW THEREFORE THIS AGREEMENT WITNESSETH AS FOLLOWS:

## 1. DEFINITIONS

1.1 "**Deliverables**" means the dashboards, data models, reports, documentation and other work product specified in a Statement of Work.

1.2 "**Fees**" means the fees set out in the applicable Statement of Work.

1.3 "**Milestone**" and "**Milestone Fee**" mean a milestone and the fee attributable to it, as specified in a Statement of Work.

1.4 "**Statement of Work**" or "**SOW**" means a document executed by both Parties describing specific services, Deliverables, Milestones and Fees.

1.5 "**Confidential Information**" means all business, technical, financial and customer information disclosed by either Party, whether oral, written or electronic, that is designated as confidential or ought reasonably to be understood as confidential.

## 2. SCOPE OF SERVICES

# MASTER SERVICES AGREEMENT

**Agreement No.:** ANHG/IT/2025/017
**Date:** 15 March 2025

## PARTIES

This Master Services Agreement (the "**Agreement**") is made on the date stated above between:

1. **AL NOOR HOSPITALITY GROUP LLC**, a limited liability company registered in the Emirate of Dubai, United Arab Emirates, having its principal office at Level 22, Al Noor Tower, Sheikh Zayed Road, PO Box 118834, Dubai, United Arab Emirates (the "**Client**"); and

2. **ATLIQ TECHNOLOGIES PRIVATE LIMITED**, a private limited company incorporated under the laws of India (CIN U72900MH2019PTC321456; GSTIN 27AAKCA4821F1Z3), having its registered office at 4th Floor, Baner Business Bay, Pune 411045, Maharashtra, India (the "**Supplier**"),

each a "**Party**" and together the "**Parties**".

## RECITALS

A. The Client owns, operates and manages a portfolio of hotels, resorts and serviced apartments in the United Arab Emirates and wishes to implement a centralised guest analytics platform across fourteen (14) of its properties.

B. The Supplier is engaged in the business of providing software development, data engineering, analytics and artificial intelligence services and has represented that it has the skills and resources to deliver such platform.

C. The Parties wish to set out the terms on which the Supplier will provide the Services to the Client, including certain restrictions reasonably necessary to protect the Client's commercially sensitive information and competitive position.

NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the mutual covenants set out below, the Parties agree as follows:

## 1. DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATION

1.1 In this Agreement, unless the context otherwise requires, capitalised terms have the meanings given below.

1.2 "**Affiliate**" means, in relation to a Party, any entity that directly or indirectly controls, is controlled by, or is under common control with that Party, where "control" means the ownership of more than fifty percent (50%) of the voting securities of an entity or the power to direct its management and policies, whether by contract or otherwise.

1.3 "**Business Day**" means a day other than a Friday, Saturday or public holiday in Dubai.

1.4 "**Client Data**" means all data, including Guest Data, reservation, occupancy, pricing and revenue data, supplied by or on behalf of the Client or generated by the Platform in the course of the Services.

1.5 "**Confidential Information**" has the meaning given in Clause 8.1.

1.6 "**Deliverables**" means all documents, software, dashboards, models, reports and other materials delivered by the Supplier to the Client under an SOW.

1.7 "**Effective Date**" means 15 March 2025.

1.8 "**Fees**" means the fees payable by the Client for the Services as set out in Clause 5 and the applicable SOW.

1.9 "**GCC**" means the member states of the Gulf Cooperation Council, being the United Arab Emirates, the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, the State of Qatar, the State of Kuwait, the Kingdom of Bahrain and the Sultanate of Oman.

1.10 "**Guest Data**" means any personal data relating to guests, prospective guests or loyalty members of the Client.

1.11 "**Hospitality Business**" means any person, firm or entity that owns, operates, manages or franchises hotels, resorts or serviced apartments, or that provides distribution, revenue-management or guest-analytics services to any such person, firm or entity.

1.12 "**Milestone**" means a delivery milestone specified in an SOW.

1.13 "**Platform**" means the guest analytics platform to be designed, built and deployed by the Supplier for the Client as described in SOW-1.

1.14 "**Restricted Period**" means the Term and the period of eighteen (18) months following the expiry or termination of this Agreement.

1.15 "**Services**" means the services described in this Agreement and each SOW.

1.16 "**SOW**" means a statement of work executed by both Parties referencing this Agreement.

1.17 Clause headings are for convenience only. References to "including" mean "including without limitation". The singular includes the plural and vice versa.

## 2. APPOINTMENT AND SCOPE

2.1 The Client appoints the Supplier to provide the Services, and the Supplier agrees to provide the Services, on the terms of this Agreement and each SOW.

2.2 The initial SOW ("**SOW-1**") is attached as Schedule 1 and covers the design, build, deployment and hypercare of the Platform across the fourteen (14) properties listed in Schedule 1, including integration with the Client's property management system, central reservation system and loyalty database, guest segmentation models, and executive dashboards.

2.3 In the event of a conflict between this Agreement and an SOW, this Agreement shall prevail unless the SOW expressly states that it overrides a specified clause of this Agreement.

## 3. CHANGE CONTROL

3.1 Either Party may request a change to an SOW by written change request. No change shall be binding unless agreed in a written change order signed by authorised representatives of both Parties.

3.2 The Supplier shall, within ten (10) Business Days of a change request, provide an impact assessment covering effort, timeline and Fees.

## 4. CLIENT OBLIGATIONS

4.1 The Client shall provide the Supplier with timely access to its systems, data, premises and personnel as reasonably required, and shall nominate a single point of contact, who shall initially be Mr. Omar Haddad, Head of Digital.

4.2 The Client shall be responsible for obtaining any third-party consents required for the Supplier to access the Client's systems.

## 5. FEES AND PAYMENT

5.1 The total Fees for SOW-1 are **USD 185,000** (one hundred and eighty-five thousand United States Dollars), payable against Milestones as set out in Schedule 1.

5.2 The Supplier shall invoice upon achievement of each Milestone. Invoices are payable within thirty (30) days of receipt.

5.3 All Fees are exclusive of VAT and any other applicable taxes. Where the Client is required by law to withhold tax, it shall provide the Supplier with the relevant withholding certificate.

5.4 Late payments shall bear interest at one percent (1%) per month from the due date until the date of payment.

5.5 The Client may dispute any invoice in good faith by written notice within ten (10) Business Days of receipt, and shall pay the undisputed portion by the due date.

## 6. TERM AND TERMINATION

6.1 This Agreement commences on the Effective Date and continues for a period of three (3) years, expiring on 14 March 2028 (the "**Term**"), unless terminated earlier in accordance with this Clause 6.

6.2 Either Party may terminate this Agreement by written notice with immediate effect if the other Party commits a material breach which, if remediable, is not remedied within thirty (30) days of written notice.

6.3 Either Party may terminate this Agreement immediately if the other Party becomes insolvent, enters into liquidation or has a receiver appointed.

6.4 The Client may terminate an SOW for convenience on sixty (60) days' written notice, subject to payment for all Services performed up to the date of termination and any non-cancellable costs.

6.5 Clauses 8, 9, 12, 14, 15, 16 and 21 shall survive expiry or termination of this Agreement.

## 7. PERSONNEL

7.1 The Supplier shall assign suitably qualified personnel and shall not replace key personnel named in an SOW without the Client's prior consent, not to be unreasonably withheld.

7.2 Supplier personnel attending the Client's premises shall comply with the Client's site, health and safety and information security policies.

## 8. CONFIDENTIALITY

8.1 "**Confidential Information**" means all information disclosed by one Party to the other, whether before or after the Effective Date, that is marked confidential or would reasonably be regarded as confidential, including Client Data, pricing strategies, rate plans, occupancy forecasts and business plans.

8.2 Each Party shall keep the other's Confidential Information confidential, use it only for the purposes of this Agreement, and disclose it only to its employees and advisers who need to know it and are bound by equivalent obligations.

8.3 These obligations do not apply to information that is public other than through breach, was lawfully known before disclosure, is independently developed, or is required to be disclosed by law.

8.4 The obligations in this Clause 8 continue for five (5) years after expiry or termination.

## 9. INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY

9.1 Upon payment in full of the relevant Fees, all intellectual property rights in the Deliverables created specifically for the Client shall vest in the Client.

9.2 The Supplier retains ownership of its pre-existing tools, libraries, methodologies and know-how ("**Supplier Background IP**"). To the extent any Supplier Background IP is incorporated into a Deliverable, the Supplier grants the Client a perpetual, non-exclusive, royalty-free licence to use it as part of that Deliverable.

## 10. DELIVERY, ACCEPTANCE AND LIQUIDATED DAMAGES

10.1 The Supplier shall use all reasonable endeavours to achieve each Milestone by the date set out in the relevant SOW.

10.2 Each Deliverable shall be subject to acceptance testing by the Client within ten (10) Business Days of delivery against the acceptance criteria in the SOW. Deliverables not rejected in writing within that period shall be deemed accepted.

10.3 If the Supplier fails to achieve a Milestone by its due date for reasons attributable to the Supplier, the Supplier shall pay to the Client, as liquidated damages, one percent (1%) of the Fees payable for the affected Milestone for each complete week of delay, provided that the aggregate liquidated damages payable under this Agreement shall not exceed ten percent (10%) of the total Fees payable under this Agreement.

10.4 The Parties agree that the liquidated damages in Clause 10.3 are a genuine pre-estimate of loss. No liquidated damages shall be payable for delay caused by the Client, its contractors, or a Force Majeure Event.

## 11. WARRANTIES

11.1 The Supplier warrants that the Services will be performed with reasonable skill and care in accordance with good industry practice, and that the Deliverables will materially conform to their specifications for ninety (90) days after acceptance.

11.2 Each Party warrants that it has full power and authority to enter into this Agreement.

11.3 Except as expressly set out in this Agreement, all other warranties are excluded to the extent permitted by law.

## 12. RESTRICTIVE COVENANTS

12.1 In consideration of the Client disclosing to the Supplier its Confidential Information, including its revenue strategies, pricing models and Guest Data, the Supplier undertakes that neither it nor any of its Affiliates shall, during the Restricted Period, directly or indirectly, provide data analytics, artificial intelligence or revenue-management services to any Hospitality Business in the GCC.

12.2 For the purposes of Clause 12.1, services are provided "in the GCC" if the Hospitality Business receiving them is headquartered in, or the services relate to properties or operations located in, any state of the GCC, irrespective of where the services are performed.

12.3 The Supplier shall procure that each of its Affiliates complies with this Clause 12 as if it were a party to this Agreement, and any breach by an Affiliate shall be deemed a breach by the Supplier.

12.4 The Client may, in its sole discretion, waive the restriction in Clause 12.1 in respect of a specific engagement by written consent signed by an authorised signatory of the Client. Any such waiver shall be limited to its express terms.

12.5 During the Term and for twelve (12) months thereafter, neither Party shall solicit for employment any employee of the other Party who was directly involved in the Services, save through general advertisements not targeted at such employees.

12.6 The Supplier acknowledges that the restrictions in this Clause 12 are reasonable in scope, duration and geography and are necessary to protect the legitimate interests of the Client.

## 13. SUBCONTRACTING

13.1 The Supplier shall not subcontract any part of the Services without the Client's prior written consent. The Supplier remains responsible for the acts and omissions of its subcontractors.

## 14. LIMITATION OF LIABILITY

14.1 Neither Party shall be liable for any indirect, consequential or special loss, or for loss of profits, revenue, goodwill or anticipated savings.

14.2 Subject to Clause 14.3, each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or in connection with this Agreement shall not exceed an amount equal to the Fees paid by the Client to the Supplier in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim.

14.3 Nothing in this Agreement limits liability for fraud, wilful misconduct, breach of Clause 8 (Confidentiality), or death or personal injury caused by negligence.

## 15. INDEMNITY

15.1 The Supplier shall indemnify the Client against losses arising from any third-party claim that the Deliverables (excluding Client materials) infringe that third party's intellectual property rights.

15.2 The Client shall indemnify the Supplier against losses arising from any third-party claim that Client Data or Client materials infringe that third party's rights.

15.3 The indemnified Party shall promptly notify the indemnifying Party, allow it conduct of the defence, and provide reasonable assistance.

## 16. DATA PROTECTION

16.1 Each Party shall comply with applicable data protection laws, including the DIFC Data Protection Law No. 5 of 2020 and the UAE Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021, to the extent applicable.

16.2 The Supplier shall process Guest Data only on the documented instructions of the Client, implement appropriate technical and organisational measures, and notify the Client without undue delay (and in any event within forty-eight (48) hours) of any personal data breach.

16.3 The Supplier shall not transfer Guest Data outside the UAE without the Client's prior written consent. Any Guest Data accessed from India shall be accessed remotely from UAE-hosted environments only.

## 17. INSURANCE

17.1 The Supplier shall maintain professional indemnity insurance of not less than USD 500,000 per claim for the Term and one (1) year thereafter.

## 18. FORCE MAJEURE

18.1 Neither Party shall be liable for delay or failure caused by events beyond its reasonable control (a "**Force Majeure Event**"), provided it notifies the other Party promptly. If a Force Majeure Event continues for more than sixty (60) days, either Party may terminate the affected SOW.

## 19. ASSIGNMENT

19.1 Neither Party may assign this Agreement without the prior written consent of the other, except that the Client may assign to an Affiliate on written notice.

## 20. NOTICES

20.1 Notices shall be in writing and delivered by hand, courier or email to: (a) Client: Attn. Head of Digital, Level 22, Al Noor Tower, Sheikh Zayed Road, Dubai, with copy to legal@alnoorhospitality.ae; (b) Supplier: Attn. Chief Executive Officer, 4th Floor, Baner Business Bay, Pune 411045, India, with copy to karandeep@atliq.com.

## 21. GOVERNING LAW AND DISPUTE RESOLUTION

21.1 This Agreement and any non-contractual obligations arising out of it shall be governed by the laws of the Dubai International Financial Centre.

21.2 The Parties shall first attempt to resolve any dispute through good-faith negotiation between senior executives for thirty (30) days.

21.3 Failing resolution, the courts of the Dubai International Financial Centre shall have exclusive jurisdiction.

## 22. GENERAL

22.1 This Agreement, together with its Schedules and SOWs, constitutes the entire agreement between the Parties and supersedes all prior discussions.

22.2 No amendment shall be effective unless in writing and signed by both Parties. No failure or delay in exercising any right shall operate as a waiver.

22.3 If any provision is held invalid, the remainder shall continue in effect, and the invalid provision shall be deemed modified to the minimum extent necessary to make it enforceable.

22.4 The Parties are independent contractors. This Agreement may be executed in counterparts and by electronic signature.

# STRATEGIC PARTNERSHIP AGREEMENT

## PARTIES

This Strategic Partnership Agreement (the "**Agreement**") is made between:

1. **CLOUDSPAN TECHNOLOGIES PTE. LTD.**, a company incorporated in Singapore (UEN 201834567K), having its registered office at 8 Marina View, #29-01 Asia Square Tower 1, Singapore 018960 ("**CloudSpan**"); and

each a "**Party**" and together the "**Parties**".

## RECITALS

A. CloudSpan provides the CloudSpan Platform, a cloud lakehouse and data-warehouse platform offered as a service.

B. Partner provides software, data engineering, analytics, business intelligence and AI/ML services to enterprise customers.

C. The Parties wish to establish a strategic relationship under which Partner will implement the CloudSpan Platform for customers and refer prospective customers to CloudSpan, on the terms of this Agreement.

## 1. DEFINITIONS

1.1 "**Affiliate**" means, in relation to a Party, any entity that directly or indirectly controls, is controlled by, or is under common control with that Party, where "control" means ownership of more than fifty per cent (50%) of the voting securities or the power to direct management.

1.2 "**CloudSpan Platform**" means CloudSpan's cloud lakehouse and data-warehouse service, together with associated tools, connectors and documentation made generally available by CloudSpan from time to time.

1.3 "**Customer**" means a third party that subscribes to the CloudSpan Platform directly from CloudSpan.

1.4 "**Referred Customer**" means a Customer introduced by Partner through a Referral Registration accepted by CloudSpan under Clause 4.

1.5 "**Referral Registration**" means a registration of a prospective customer submitted by Partner through the CloudSpan Partner Portal.

1.6 "**First-Year Subscription Fees**" means the subscription fees actually received by CloudSpan from a Referred Customer for the first twelve (12) months of its initial subscription, excluding taxes, professional services fees, usage overages billed separately and refunds or credits.

1.7 "**Certified Engineer**" means an employee of Partner who holds a current CloudSpan Certified Implementation Engineer credential.

1.8 "**Implementation Services**" means services provided by Partner to Customers for the design, migration, configuration, integration and deployment of solutions on the CloudSpan Platform.

1.9 "**Competing Platform**" has the meaning given in Clause 7.2.

1.10 "**Territory**" means the Republic of India and the member states of the Gulf Cooperation Council, being the United Arab Emirates, the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, the State of Qatar, the State of Kuwait, the Kingdom of Bahrain and the Sultanate of Oman.

1.11 "**Marks**" means a Party's trade names, trade marks, logos and partner badges.

## 2. APPOINTMENT

2.1 CloudSpan appoints Partner as a Premier Implementation and Referral Partner for the CloudSpan Platform. Partner accepts the appointment.

2.2 Save as provided in Clause 7, the appointment is non-exclusive. CloudSpan may appoint other partners in any territory, and Partner may operate outside the Territory without restriction.

2.3 Partner is not appointed as a reseller. Customers contract with and pay CloudSpan directly for subscriptions to the CloudSpan Platform.

## 3. PARTNER COMMITMENTS

3.1 Partner shall maintain, throughout the Term, not fewer than four (4) Certified Engineers. Where the number falls below four (4) for reasons outside Partner's reasonable control, Partner shall have ninety (90) days to restore it.

3.2 Partner shall deliver Implementation Services with reasonable skill and care, in accordance with CloudSpan's published implementation guidelines, and shall be solely responsible to Customers for Implementation Services it contracts to provide.

3.3 Partner shall not make any representation or warranty concerning the CloudSpan Platform beyond those contained in CloudSpan's published documentation.

3.4 Partner shall participate in a joint business-planning review with CloudSpan at least once every six (6) months.

## 4. REFERRALS AND REFERRAL FEES

4.1 Partner may submit Referral Registrations for prospective customers. CloudSpan shall accept or reject each Referral Registration within ten (10) business days. A registration shall be rejected only where the prospect is an existing Customer or is already the subject of an active opportunity registered by CloudSpan or another partner in the preceding ninety (90) days.

4.2 An accepted Referral Registration shall remain valid for one hundred and eighty (180) days. If the prospect signs a subscription order with CloudSpan within that period, it becomes a Referred Customer.

4.3 CloudSpan shall pay Partner a referral fee equal to twelve per cent (12%) of the First-Year Subscription Fees received from each Referred Customer (the "**Referral Fee**").

4.4 CloudSpan shall provide Partner with a quarterly statement of Referral Fees within fifteen (15) days of the end of each calendar quarter. Partner shall invoice CloudSpan on the basis of that statement, and CloudSpan shall pay each undisputed invoice within thirty (30) days of receipt.

4.5 Referral Fees are exclusive of GST and other applicable taxes. Where CloudSpan is required by law to withhold tax, it shall provide Partner with the relevant certificate to enable Partner to claim credit.

4.6 Partner may, on reasonable notice and not more than once per year, have CloudSpan's records relating to Referral Fees reviewed by an independent accountant, at Partner's cost, unless an underpayment of more than five per cent (5%) is found, in which case CloudSpan shall bear the cost.

## 5. CLOUDSPAN COMMITMENTS

5.1 CloudSpan shall provide Partner with:
   (a) twenty (20) complimentary certification vouchers per contract year;
   (b) a non-production sandbox environment of the CloudSpan Platform for training and demonstration;
   (c) access to the CloudSpan Partner Portal, partner-level technical support and early-access programmes; and
   (d) a named partner manager.

5.2 CloudSpan shall list Partner in its public partner directory for the Territory and shall use reasonable efforts to refer Implementation Services opportunities in the Territory to Partner.

5.3 The Parties shall agree an annual co-marketing plan. CloudSpan shall contribute market development funds of up to USD 25,000 per contract year for jointly approved activities.

## 6. MARKETING AND USE OF MARKS

6.1 Each Party grants the other a non-exclusive, non-transferable, royalty-free licence during the Term to use its Marks solely to identify the partnership, in accordance with the owning Party's brand guidelines.

6.2 Neither Party shall issue any press release concerning this Agreement without the prior written approval of the other, not to be unreasonably withheld.

## 7. EXCLUSIVITY

7.1 In consideration of the Referral Fees, market development funds and other benefits under this Agreement, during the Term Partner and its Affiliates shall not act as an implementation, reseller or referral partner for any Competing Platform in India or the GCC.

7.2 "**Competing Platform**" means any cloud data-warehouse, lakehouse or unified analytics platform offered as a service.

7.3 For clarity, Clause 7.1 does not restrict Partner or its Affiliates from (a) providing services outside India and the GCC; or (b) providing services to a customer that has independently selected a platform, provided Partner does not hold a partner appointment with, or receive any fee or benefit from, the provider of that platform.

7.4 In this Clause 7, "GCC" has the meaning given to the member states listed in the definition of Territory.

## 8. INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY

8.1 Each Party retains all rights in its own intellectual property. CloudSpan owns the CloudSpan Platform and all improvements to it.

8.2 Partner retains all rights in its own methodologies, accelerators, tools, templates and know-how, whether developed before or during the Term, including those used in delivering Implementation Services.

8.3 Any feedback provided by Partner concerning the CloudSpan Platform may be used by CloudSpan without restriction, provided Partner's Confidential Information is not disclosed.

## 9. CONFIDENTIALITY

9.2 Clause 9.1 does not apply to information that is public other than through breach, already lawfully known, lawfully received from a third party, or independently developed, or to disclosure required by law.

9.3 The obligations in this Clause 9 survive for three (3) years after termination or expiry.

## 10. DATA PROTECTION

10.1 Each Party shall comply with data protection laws applicable to it. Where Partner processes Customer personal data in providing Implementation Services, it does so under its own agreement with that Customer.

10.2 Referral Registrations shall contain only business contact information that Partner is entitled to share.

## 11. WARRANTIES

11.1 Each Party warrants that it has full power and authority to enter into this Agreement and that doing so does not breach any other agreement binding on it.

11.2 Save as expressly stated, all warranties, conditions and representations, whether express or implied, are excluded to the extent permitted by law.

## 12. INDEMNITIES

12.1 CloudSpan shall indemnify Partner against third-party claims that the CloudSpan Platform infringes that third party's intellectual property rights.

12.2 Partner shall indemnify CloudSpan against third-party claims that Partner's own materials or Implementation Services infringe that third party's intellectual property rights.

12.3 The indemnified Party shall notify the other promptly of any claim, allow it conduct of the defence and provide reasonable assistance at its cost.

## 13. LIMITATION OF LIABILITY

13.1 Neither Party shall be liable for any indirect, consequential or special loss, or loss of profit, revenue or goodwill.

13.2 Each Party's aggregate liability under this Agreement in any contract year shall not exceed the greater of (a) the total Referral Fees paid or payable in the preceding twelve (12) months and (b) USD 100,000.

13.3 Clauses 13.1 and 13.2 do not apply to liability under Clause 12, breach of Clause 9, or liability that cannot be limited by law.

## 14. TERM AND TERMINATION

14.1 This Agreement commences on the Effective Date and continues for three (3) years, until 31 August 2028 (the "**Term**"), unless terminated earlier. The Parties may renew it by written agreement.

14.2 Either Party may terminate this Agreement for convenience by giving not less than ninety (90) days' written notice to the other.

## 15. GOVERNING LAW AND DISPUTE RESOLUTION

15.1 This Agreement is governed by the laws of the Republic of Singapore.

15.2 The Parties shall first attempt to resolve any dispute through good-faith discussions between senior executives for thirty (30) days.

15.3 Any dispute not so resolved shall be referred to and finally resolved by arbitration administered by the Singapore International Arbitration Centre ("**SIAC**") under the SIAC Rules in force at the time. # BUSINESS ASSOCIATE AGREEMENT

**CareBridge Clinics, Inc. — BAA No. CBC-BAA-2025-014**

This Business Associate Agreement (this "**BAA**") is entered into as of October 6, 2025 (the "**BAA Effective Date**") by and between **CareBridge Clinics, Inc.**, an Arizona corporation with its principal place of business at 2200 North Central Avenue, Suite 900, Phoenix, Arizona 85004 ("**Covered Entity**"), and **AtliQ Inc**, a Delaware corporation with its principal place of business at 101 College Road East, Suite 210, Princeton, New Jersey 08540 ("**Business Associate**"). Covered Entity and Business Associate are each a "**Party**" and together the "**Parties**."

## RECITALS

A. Covered Entity and Business Associate are parties to a Master Services Agreement dated as of October 6, 2025 (together with its Statements of Work, the "**Master Services Agreement**"), under which Business Associate provides patient-scheduling analytics services to Covered Entity (the "**Services**").

B. In performing the Services, Business Associate may create, receive, maintain or transmit Protected Health Information on behalf of Covered Entity, and the Parties wish to comply with the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act of 1996, the Health Information Technology for Economic and Clinical Health Act, and their implementing regulations at 45 C.F.R. Parts 160 and 164 (collectively, "**HIPAA**").

NOW, THEREFORE, the Parties agree as follows:

## 1. DEFINITIONS

1.1 Capitalized terms used but not defined in this BAA have the meanings given in HIPAA, including "Breach," "Data Aggregation," "Designated Record Set," "Individual," "Required By Law," "Secretary," "Security Incident," "Subcontractor" and "Unsecured Protected Health Information."

1.2 "**Protected Health Information**" or "**PHI**" has the meaning given in 45 C.F.R. § 160.103, limited to information created, received, maintained or transmitted by Business Associate on behalf of Covered Entity.

1.3 "**De-identified Data**" means health information that has been de-identified in accordance with 45 C.F.R. § 164.514(b) and that is therefore not PHI.

1.4 "**Covered Entity Environment**" means the cloud tenant, virtual desktops and other systems owned or controlled by Covered Entity and hosted in the United States, to which Covered Entity grants Business Associate access for the Services.

## 2. PERMITTED USES AND DISCLOSURES

2.1 **Services.** Business Associate may use and disclose PHI only as necessary to perform the Services under the Master Services Agreement, and as otherwise permitted or required by this BAA or as Required By Law.

2.2 **Minimum Necessary.** Business Associate shall limit its uses, disclosures and requests of PHI to the minimum necessary to accomplish the intended purpose, in accordance with 45 C.F.R. § 164.502(b).

2.3 **Management and Administration.** Business Associate may use PHI for its proper management and administration or to carry out its legal responsibilities, and may disclose PHI for those purposes if the disclosure is Required By Law, or Business Associate obtains reasonable written assurances from the recipient that the PHI will be held confidentially, used or further disclosed only as Required By Law or for the purpose for which it was disclosed, and that the recipient will notify Business Associate of any instance in which the confidentiality of the PHI has been breached.

2.4 **De-identification.** Business Associate may de-identify PHI in accordance with 45 C.F.R. § 164.514(b) solely for the purpose of performing the Services. De-identified Data may be used only for the Services and not for any other client, product or purpose.

2.5 **Data Aggregation.** Business Associate shall not perform Data Aggregation services unless expressly requested in writing by Covered Entity.

2.6 **No Sale; No Marketing.** Business Associate shall not sell PHI or use or disclose PHI for marketing purposes.

2.7 **Prohibited Uses.** Business Associate shall not use or disclose PHI in any manner that would violate Subpart E of 45 C.F.R. Part 164 if done by Covered Entity.

## 3. LOCATION OF PHI AND OFFSHORE ACCESS

3.1 Business Associate shall access, store and process PHI only within the Covered Entity Environment, and only through personnel of Business Associate who are located in the United States and who have been identified to Covered Entity by name in writing.

3.2 Personnel of Business Associate or of any Subcontractor located outside the United States may access De-identified Data only, and only within the Covered Entity Environment or a secure environment approved in writing by Covered Entity. No PHI shall be accessed, stored or processed outside the United States.

3.3 Business Associate shall maintain, and provide to Covered Entity on request, a current list of personnel with access to PHI.

## 4. SAFEGUARDS

4.1 Business Associate shall use appropriate administrative, physical and technical safeguards, and comply with Subpart C of 45 C.F.R. Part 164 with respect to electronic PHI, to prevent use or disclosure of PHI other than as provided by this BAA.

4.2 Without limiting Section 4.1, Business Associate shall (a) encrypt electronic PHI in transit and at rest consistent with guidance issued by the Secretary; (b) require multi-factor authentication for access to PHI; (c) maintain audit logs of access to PHI; and (d) provide HIPAA privacy and security training to its personnel with access to PHI before access is granted and annually thereafter.

## 5. REPORTING

5.1 **Breaches and Non-Permitted Uses.** Business Associate shall report to Covered Entity any use or disclosure of PHI not provided for by this BAA, including any Breach of Unsecured PHI, without unreasonable delay and in no case later than five (5) business days after discovery. A Breach shall be treated as discovered as of the first day on which it is known, or by exercising reasonable diligence would have been known, to Business Associate.

5.2 **Content.** The report shall include, to the extent then known, the identity of each Individual affected, a description of the incident, the PHI involved, and the steps taken to mitigate it. Business Associate shall supplement the report as further information becomes available.

5.3 **Security Incidents.** Business Associate shall report successful Security Incidents in accordance with Section 5.1. The Parties agree that this Section constitutes notice of the ongoing existence of unsuccessful Security Incidents (such as pings, port scans and blocked log-in attempts) for which no further notice is required.

5.4 **Mitigation and Notification.** Business Associate shall mitigate, to the extent practicable, any harmful effect of a use or disclosure in violation of this BAA. Covered Entity shall determine whether notification to Individuals, the Secretary or the media is required and shall control the content of any such notification. Business Associate shall reimburse Covered Entity's reasonable, documented costs of notification and credit monitoring to the extent the Breach was caused by Business Associate or its Subcontractors, subject to Section 9.

## 6. SUBCONTRACTORS

6.1 Business Associate shall ensure, in accordance with 45 C.F.R. §§ 164.502(e)(1)(ii) and 164.308(b)(2), that any Subcontractor that creates, receives, maintains or transmits PHI on behalf of Business Associate agrees in a written business associate agreement to the same restrictions, conditions and requirements that apply to Business Associate under this BAA, including Section 3.

6.2 Business Associate shall notify Covered Entity in writing of any Subcontractor engaged in connection with the Services and shall remain responsible for the performance of its Subcontractors.

## 7. INDIVIDUAL RIGHTS

7.1 **Access.** Within ten (10) business days of a request by Covered Entity, Business Associate shall make PHI in a Designated Record Set available to Covered Entity as necessary for Covered Entity to meet its obligations under 45 C.F.R. § 164.524.

7.2 **Amendment.** Within ten (10) business days of a request by Covered Entity, Business Associate shall make any amendment to PHI in a Designated Record Set as directed by Covered Entity under 45 C.F.R. § 164.526.

7.3 **Accounting.** Business Associate shall document disclosures of PHI and provide to Covered Entity, within fifteen (15) business days of request, the information required for Covered Entity to respond to a request for an accounting under 45 C.F.R. § 164.528.

7.4 Business Associate shall forward to Covered Entity within five (5) business days any request it receives directly from an Individual under this Section 7.

## 8. OTHER OBLIGATIONS

8.1 **Books and Records.** Business Associate shall make its internal practices, books and records relating to the use and disclosure of PHI available to the Secretary for purposes of determining compliance with HIPAA.

8.2 **Covered Entity Obligations.** To the extent Business Associate carries out an obligation of Covered Entity under Subpart E of 45 C.F.R. Part 164, Business Associate shall comply with the requirements of Subpart E that apply to Covered Entity in the performance of that obligation.

8.3 **Covered Entity Responsibilities.** Covered Entity shall (a) notify Business Associate of any limitation in its notice of privacy practices, any change in or revocation of an Individual's permission, and any restriction agreed under 45 C.F.R. § 164.522, to the extent it affects Business Associate's use or disclosure of PHI; (b) disclose to Business Associate only the minimum PHI necessary for the Services; and (c) not request Business Associate to use or disclose PHI in any manner not permissible under HIPAA.

8.4 **Assessment.** Upon thirty (30) days' written notice, and not more than once in any twelve (12) month period unless following a Breach, Covered Entity may request reasonable documentation (including a completed security questionnaire and relevant policies) to verify Business Associate's compliance with this BAA.

## 9. LIABILITY

9.1 Each Party's liability arising out of or relating to this BAA, including any Breach, is subject to the limitations and exclusions of liability in the Master Services Agreement, under which aggregate liability for claims relating to a Breach or a violation of this BAA shall not exceed two (2) times the Fees paid or payable under the Master Services Agreement in the twelve (12) months preceding the event giving rise to the claim.

## 10. TERM AND TERMINATION

10.1 **Term.** This BAA commences on the BAA Effective Date and continues until the Master Services Agreement expires or is terminated, subject to Section 10.4.

10.2 **Termination for Cause.** If either Party determines that the other has materially breached this BAA, it shall give written notice and a thirty (30) day period to cure. If the breach is not cured within that period, the non-breaching Party may terminate this BAA and the affected portions of the Master Services Agreement.

10.3 **Return or Destruction.** On termination or expiry, Business Associate shall, within thirty (30) days, return to Covered Entity or destroy all PHI in its possession or in the possession of its Subcontractors, and certify the destruction in writing. If return or destruction is infeasible, Business Associate shall notify Covered Entity of the conditions that make it infeasible, extend the protections of this BAA to that PHI, and limit further uses and disclosures to those purposes that make return or destruction infeasible, for so long as Business Associate maintains the PHI.

10.4 **Survival.** Section 10.3 and the obligations of Business Associate with respect to any PHI retained under it survive termination.

## 11. GENERAL

11.1 **Amendment.** The Parties shall amend this BAA as necessary to comply with any change in HIPAA. No other amendment is effective unless in writing and signed by both Parties.

11.2 **Interpretation.** Any ambiguity in this BAA shall be resolved to permit compliance with HIPAA. In the event of conflict between this BAA and the Master Services Agreement with respect to PHI, this BAA controls; in all other respects the Master Services Agreement controls.

11.3 **No Third-Party Beneficiaries.** Nothing in this BAA confers any rights on any person other than the Parties.

11.4 **Governing Law.** This BAA is governed by the laws of the State of Arizona, except to the extent preempted by federal law, and disputes shall be resolved as provided in the Master Services Agreement.

11.5 **Counterparts.** This BAA may be executed in counterparts and by electronic signature.

Harrington shall not disclose, and AtliQ shall not request, Protected Health Information under this Agreement.

## 3. OBLIGATIONS

3.1 Each Receiving Party shall (a) use the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information solely for the Purpose; (b) disclose it only to its and its Affiliates' employees, contractors and professional advisers who need to know it for the Purpose and are bound by written confidentiality obligations no less protective than this Agreement; (c) protect it with at least the degree of care it uses for its own confidential information of like kind, and no less than reasonable care; and (d) promptly notify the Disclosing Party of any unauthorized use or disclosure of which it becomes aware.

3.2 Each Party is responsible for any breach of this Agreement by persons to whom it discloses Confidential Information.

3.3 A Receiving Party may disclose Confidential Information to the extent required by law or court order, provided it gives the Disclosing Party prompt prior written notice (where lawful) and reasonable cooperation in seeking a protective order, and discloses only the portion legally required.

## 4. RETURN OR DESTRUCTION

4.1 Upon the Disclosing Party's written request, the Receiving Party shall promptly return or destroy the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information and confirm destruction in writing, except for copies retained in automatic backup systems or as required by law, which remain subject to this Agreement.

## 5. TERM

5.1 This Agreement applies to disclosures made during the two (2) years following the Effective Date. Either Party may terminate it earlier on thirty (30) days' written notice.

5.2 Each Party's obligations under Sections 3 and 4 continue for three (3) years after the end of the disclosure period, and, with respect to trade secrets, for as long as the information remains a trade secret under applicable law.

6.1 All Confidential Information remains the property of the Disclosing Party. No license is granted except as expressly stated.

6.2 Confidential Information is provided "AS IS." Neither Party is obligated to proceed with any transaction by reason of this Agreement.

## 7. REMEDIES

7.1 Each Party acknowledges that unauthorized disclosure may cause irreparable harm for which damages would be an inadequate remedy, and that the Disclosing Party may seek injunctive relief in addition to any other remedy, without posting bond.

## 8. GENERAL

8.1 **Governing Law; Venue.** This Agreement is governed by the laws of the State of Texas, without regard to its conflict of laws principles. Any action arising out of this Agreement shall be brought in the state or federal courts located in Harris County, Texas.
