# MASTER PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT

**Harrington Health Systems, Inc. — Contract No. HHS-IT-2026-0193**
**Form: HHS Vendor MPSA (Rev. 07/2026)**

This Master Professional Services Agreement (together with all Exhibits, Statements of Work and amendments hereto, this "**Agreement**") is entered into as of the date of the last signature below (the "**Effective Date**") by and between **Harrington Health Systems, Inc.**, a Texas nonprofit corporation with its principal place of business at 6400 Fannin Street, Suite 1800, Houston, Texas 77030 ("**Harrington**" or "**Client**"), and **AtliQ Inc**, a Delaware corporation with its principal place of business at 101 College Road East, Suite 210, Princeton, New Jersey 08540 ("**Contractor**"). Client and Contractor are each a "**Party**" and collectively the "**Parties**."

## RECITALS

WHEREAS, Client operates an integrated health system comprising acute care hospitals, ambulatory surgery centers, and outpatient clinics in the greater Houston metropolitan area;

WHEREAS, Client desires to engage Contractor to design and implement an enterprise clinical and operational analytics platform, and Contractor desires to provide such services, subject to the terms and conditions of this Agreement;

NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the mutual covenants and agreements set forth herein, and for other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, the Parties agree as follows:

## ARTICLE 1 — DEFINITIONS

1.1 "**Affiliate**" means any entity that directly or indirectly controls, is controlled by, or is under common control with a Party.
1.2 "**Applicable Law**" means all federal, state and local laws, rules, regulations, ordinances and binding guidance applicable to a Party or the Services, including HIPAA, the HITECH Act, the Texas Medical Records Privacy Act (Tex. Health & Safety Code ch. 181), and the Anti-Kickback Statute.
1.3 "**Business Associate Agreement**" or "**BAA**" means the business associate agreement attached hereto as Exhibit D.
1.4 "**Client Materials**" means all data, information, systems access, documents and other materials furnished by or on behalf of Client.
1.5 "**Contractor Personnel**" means all employees, agents, subcontractors and independent contractors of Contractor or its subcontractors who perform any portion of the Services.
1.6 "**Deliverables**" means all work product, documentation, software, code, models, reports, dashboards, data pipelines, configurations and other materials prepared, developed or delivered by or on behalf of Contractor under this Agreement, in whole or in part.
1.7 "**Delivery Date**" means each date for delivery or completion of a Deliverable or Milestone set forth in an applicable SOW.
1.8 "**Fees**" means the amounts payable to Contractor as set forth in an SOW.
1.9 "**Losses**" means any and all losses, damages, liabilities, deficiencies, claims, actions, judgments, settlements, interest, awards, penalties, fines, costs or expenses of whatever kind, including reasonable attorneys' fees.
1.10 "**PHI**" has the meaning given to "protected health information" under 45 C.F.R. § 160.103.
1.11 "**Pre-Existing Materials**" means any software, tools, libraries, frameworks, templates, methodologies, accelerators, know-how and other materials owned or licensed by Contractor prior to the Effective Date or developed independently of this Agreement.
1.12 "**Services**" means the services described in Article 2 and in each SOW.
1.13 "**SOW**" means a statement of work executed by the Parties that references this Agreement.
1.14 "**Total Contract Value**" means the aggregate Fees payable under this Agreement and all SOWs issued hereunder, which as of the Effective Date is Two Hundred Ten Thousand U.S. Dollars ($210,000.00).

## ARTICLE 2 — SERVICES

2.1 **Scope.** Contractor shall perform the Services described in the initial SOW attached as Exhibit A (the "**Initial SOW**"), which include: (a) design and build of a cloud data platform consolidating data from Client's electronic health record, patient accounting, scheduling and workforce management systems; (b) development of operational dashboards for bed management, emergency department throughput, operating room utilization and staffing; (c) a readmission-risk predictive model for use by Client's care management team; and (d) knowledge transfer to Client's Enterprise Analytics department.
2.2 **Additional SOWs.** The Parties may from time to time execute additional SOWs. Each SOW shall be governed by this Agreement. In the event of a conflict between this Agreement and an SOW, this Agreement shall control unless the SOW expressly states the specific Section of this Agreement it is intended to modify.
2.3 **Standards of Performance.** Contractor shall perform the Services in a diligent, professional and workmanlike manner, in accordance with the highest standards of the industry, and in compliance with Applicable Law and Client's policies made available to Contractor, as updated from time to time.
2.4 **Contractor Personnel.** Contractor shall assign qualified Contractor Personnel. Client may, in its sole discretion, request removal of any Contractor Personnel, and Contractor shall promptly replace such individual at no additional cost to Client. Contractor Personnel accessing Client facilities or systems shall complete Client's background check, drug screening, immunization and compliance training requirements.
2.5 **Subcontracting.** Contractor shall not subcontract any portion of the Services without Client's prior written consent. Contractor shall remain fully responsible for any subcontractor's performance.
2.6 **Client Cooperation.** Client shall use reasonable efforts to provide Contractor with access to Client Materials reasonably necessary for the performance of the Services.
2.7 **Change Orders.** No change in the scope of Services shall be binding unless set forth in a written change order executed by authorized representatives of both Parties.

## ARTICLE 3 — ACCEPTANCE

3.1 Client shall have thirty (30) days following delivery of each Deliverable to test and evaluate such Deliverable against the acceptance criteria in the applicable SOW.
3.2 If Client determines that a Deliverable does not conform, Client shall notify Contractor, and Contractor shall correct the non-conformity at no cost within ten (10) business days. Client may repeat the acceptance process until the Deliverable conforms, or may, at its option, reject the Deliverable and receive a refund of all Fees paid in respect thereof.
3.3 Acceptance shall not be deemed to occur by use in production, by payment, or by the passage of time.

## ARTICLE 4 — FEES, INVOICING AND PAYMENT

4.1 **Fees.** Client shall pay Contractor the Fees set forth in each SOW. Fees are firm and fixed and shall not be increased during the term of the applicable SOW.
4.2 **Invoices.** Contractor shall invoice Client monthly in arrears for Deliverables accepted in the preceding month. Each invoice shall reference the Contract No. and SOW number, and be submitted through Client's supplier portal. Invoices not submitted within ninety (90) days after acceptance shall be deemed waived.
4.3 **Payment Terms.** Client shall pay each properly submitted, undisputed invoice within ninety (90) days after Client's receipt thereof.
4.4 **Disputed Amounts.** Client may withhold payment of any amount it disputes in good faith. Contractor shall continue performing the Services during the pendency of any dispute.
4.5 **Set-off.** Client may set off against any amount owed to Contractor any amount owed by Contractor to Client under this Agreement or any other agreement.
4.6 **Expenses.** Client shall reimburse only pre-approved, reasonable travel expenses incurred in accordance with Client's Vendor Travel Policy (Exhibit C).
4.7 **Taxes.** Client is exempt from certain sales and use taxes and shall provide an exemption certificate upon request. Contractor shall be responsible for all taxes based on its income or personnel.

## ARTICLE 5 — TERM AND TERMINATION

5.1 **Term.** This Agreement shall commence on the Effective Date and continue for three (3) years, unless earlier terminated as provided herein. Each SOW shall remain in effect for the period stated therein.
5.2 **Termination for Cause.** Either Party may terminate this Agreement or any SOW upon written notice if the other Party materially breaches this Agreement and fails to cure such breach within thirty (30) days after written notice thereof.
5.3 **Termination for Convenience.** Client may terminate this Agreement or any SOW, in whole or in part, for any reason or no reason, upon seven (7) days' written notice to Contractor. Upon such termination, Client's sole obligation shall be to pay Fees for Deliverables accepted by Client prior to the effective date of termination; Client shall have no obligation to pay for work in progress, unaccepted Deliverables, demobilization costs or anticipated profits.
5.4 **Termination for Regulatory Reasons.** Client may terminate immediately if Contractor or any Contractor Personnel is excluded from participation in any federal health care program.
5.5 **Effect of Termination.** Upon expiration or termination, Contractor shall (a) immediately deliver to Client all Deliverables, whether complete or incomplete, and all Client Materials; (b) provide transition assistance as reasonably requested by Client for up to ninety (90) days at the rates in the applicable SOW; and (c) certify in writing the return or destruction of all PHI in accordance with the BAA.
5.6 **Survival.** Articles 6, 7, 9, 10, 11, 12, 14 and 15 shall survive expiration or termination.

## ARTICLE 6 — CONFIDENTIALITY

6.1 "**Confidential Information**" means all non-public information disclosed by a Party, including business plans, financial information, patient information, trade secrets and Client Materials.
6.2 Each Party shall (a) hold the other Party's Confidential Information in strict confidence, (b) use it only to perform or receive the Services, and (c) disclose it only to those employees and contractors with a need to know who are bound by written obligations at least as protective.
6.3 The foregoing obligations shall not apply to information that (a) is or becomes publicly available through no fault of the receiving Party; (b) was rightfully known without restriction prior to disclosure; (c) is rightfully received from a third party without restriction; or (d) is independently developed without use of the disclosing Party's Confidential Information.
6.4 A receiving Party may disclose Confidential Information to the extent required by law, provided it gives prompt prior notice (where legally permitted) and cooperates in seeking protective treatment.
6.5 Contractor acknowledges that any breach of this Article may cause irreparable harm for which monetary damages would be inadequate, and that Client shall be entitled to injunctive relief without the posting of bond.

## ARTICLE 7 — INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY

7.1 **Work Made for Hire.** All Deliverables shall be deemed "works made for hire" as defined in the U.S. Copyright Act, 17 U.S.C. § 101, and shall be the sole and exclusive property of Client from creation.
7.2 **Assignment.** To the extent any Deliverable, or any Pre-Existing Materials incorporated into or necessary for the use of any Deliverable, does not qualify as a work made for hire, Contractor hereby irrevocably assigns, transfers and conveys to Client all right, title and interest therein, including all intellectual property rights, without further consideration.
7.3 **Further Assurances.** Contractor shall execute such documents and take such actions as Client may reasonably request to perfect, register or enforce Client's rights under this Article, and hereby appoints Client as its attorney-in-fact for such purpose.
7.4 **Moral Rights.** To the extent permitted by law, Contractor waives, and shall cause Contractor Personnel to waive, all moral rights in the Deliverables.
7.5 **Client Materials.** All Client Materials are and shall remain the sole property of Client. Nothing in this Agreement grants Contractor any right in Client Materials except the limited right to use them to perform the Services.
7.6 **Third-Party Components.** Contractor shall not incorporate any open-source or third-party software into any Deliverable without Client's prior written approval.

## ARTICLE 8 — REPRESENTATIONS AND WARRANTIES

8.1 Each Party represents and warrants that it is duly organized, validly existing and in good standing, and has full power and authority to enter into and perform this Agreement.
8.2 Contractor further represents and warrants that: (a) the Services shall be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; (b) the Deliverables shall conform to the specifications in the applicable SOW for a period of twelve (12) months following acceptance; (c) the Deliverables shall not infringe, misappropriate or violate any third-party intellectual property right; (d) the Deliverables shall not contain any virus, malicious code, time bomb or disabling device; (e) neither Contractor nor any Contractor Personnel is excluded, debarred or suspended from any federal health care program; and (f) Contractor shall comply with all Applicable Law.

## ARTICLE 9 — INDEMNIFICATION

# SOFTWARE DEVELOPMENT AND SERVICES AGREEMENT

**TravelHub FZ-LLC × AtliQ**

This Software Development and Services Agreement (the "**Agreement**") is entered into as of ____________ 2026 (the "**Effective Date**").

## 1. PARTIES

1.1 **TravelHub FZ-LLC**, a free zone limited liability company licensed by the Dubai Development Authority under licence no. 104772, with its office at Office 1408, Building 3, Dubai Internet City, P.O. Box 502211, Dubai, United Arab Emirates ("**TravelHub**" or "**Customer**"); and

1.2 **AtliQ Inc**, a Delaware corporation, with its principal office at 101 College Road East, Suite 210, Princeton, NJ 08540, USA ("**AtliQ**" or "**Developer**").

## 2. RECITALS

A. TravelHub operates a consumer travel planning app and web platform ("**TravelHub App**") that helps travellers in the Middle East plan trips, build itineraries, and book hotels, experiences and transfers with TravelHub's partners.

B. TravelHub wishes to engage AtliQ to design and build certain AI-driven features for the TravelHub App, and AtliQ is willing to do so on the terms set out below.

## 3. DEFINITIONS

3.1 "**Partner Hotels**" means hotels, resorts and serviced apartments that have entered into a commercial or commission agreement with TravelHub for the listing and booking of their inventory through the TravelHub App.
3.2 "**Deliverables**" means the software modules, models, APIs, source code, documentation and other work product described in Clause 4 and Schedule A.
3.3 "**Customer Data**" means all data provided by TravelHub or generated by users of the TravelHub App, including booking history, search behaviour and user profiles.
3.4 "**Acceptance**" means TravelHub's written confirmation that a Deliverable meets the acceptance criteria in Schedule A.
3.5 "**Background Technology**" means software, tools and know-how owned by AtliQ prior to the Effective Date or developed independently of this Agreement.

## 4. SCOPE OF WORK

4.1 AtliQ shall design, develop, test and deploy the following modules into the TravelHub App production environment:

   (a) **Itinerary Personalization Engine** — a recommendation service that generates personalised day-by-day itineraries using user preferences, trip purpose, budget, travel dates, past bookings and in-app behaviour, and re-ranks suggested activities, restaurants and experiences in real time;

   (b) **Partner Hotel Ranking Module** — a ranking and recommendation service that scores, ranks and surfaces Partner Hotels in the United Arab Emirates and the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia to TravelHub users at the point of search and itinerary building, taking into account user fit, price competitiveness, partner commission tier, availability and conversion likelihood, and that drives the sort order of hotel results and "recommended stay" placements for booking through the TravelHub App;

   (c) **Partner Performance Dashboard** — a dashboard for TravelHub's partnerships team showing impressions, click-through, bookings and commission by Partner Hotel, city and ranking position; and

   (d) **Model Operations** — deployment pipelines, monitoring and a monthly retraining process for the models in (a) and (b).

4.2 The initial launch markets for the Partner Hotel Ranking Module shall be Dubai, Abu Dhabi, Riyadh and Jeddah, with further cities in the UAE and KSA to be added by configuration.
4.3 AtliQ shall provide a technical lead and a team of engineers of appropriate seniority. AtliQ's team may work remotely but shall be available for a daily stand-up during Gulf Standard Time business hours.
4.4 TravelHub shall provide access to its cloud environment, API documentation, historical booking data and a product owner with decision-making authority.

## 5. TIMELINE AND ACCEPTANCE

5.1 AtliQ shall use commercially reasonable efforts to meet the indicative timeline in Schedule A.
5.2 TravelHub shall review each Deliverable within ten (10) business days of delivery and either confirm Acceptance or provide a written list of material non-conformities. If TravelHub fails to respond within such period, the Deliverable shall be deemed accepted.
5.3 AtliQ shall correct any notified non-conformity and re-submit the Deliverable within a reasonable time.

## 6. FEES

6.1 The total fixed fee for the Services is USD 52,000 (fifty-two thousand US dollars), payable in instalments as set out in Schedule B.
6.2 The fees are exclusive of any applicable value added tax, which, if applicable, shall be charged in addition.
6.3 Reasonable pre-approved travel expenses, if any, shall be reimbursed at cost.

## 7. INVOICING AND PAYMENT

7.1 Invoices under this Agreement shall be raised by AtliQ Technologies Pvt Ltd, GSTIN 27AAKCA4821F1Z3, on or after Acceptance of each milestone as set out in Schedule B.
7.2 TravelHub shall pay each undisputed invoice within thirty (30) days of the invoice date by wire transfer to the bank account specified on the invoice.
7.3 Late payments shall bear interest at the rate of one percent (1%) per month or the maximum rate permitted by law, whichever is lower.
7.4 Each Party shall bear its own bank charges.

## 8. TERM AND TERMINATION

8.1 This Agreement commences on the Effective Date and continues until completion of the Services and final payment, unless terminated earlier.
8.2 Either Party may terminate this Agreement upon written notice if the other Party materially breaches this Agreement and fails to cure within thirty (30) days.
8.3 TravelHub may terminate for convenience with thirty (30) days' written notice and shall pay for all work performed up to the termination date.
8.4 On termination, AtliQ shall deliver all completed and in-progress Deliverables to TravelHub.

## 9. CONFIDENTIALITY

9.1 Each Party agrees to keep the other's non-public business, technical and financial information confidential and use it solely for the purposes of this Agreement.
9.2 These obligations do not apply to information that is publicly available, independently developed, or lawfully received from a third party.
9.3 This Clause survives for three (3) years after termination.

## 10. INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY

10.1 Upon full payment, TravelHub shall own all right, title and interest in the Deliverables developed specifically for TravelHub, including the trained models and model weights for the Itinerary Personalization Engine and Partner Hotel Ranking Module.
10.2 AtliQ retains ownership of its Background Technology and grants TravelHub a perpetual, non-exclusive, royalty-free licence to use any Background Technology incorporated in the Deliverables as part of the TravelHub App.
10.3 TravelHub retains all rights in Customer Data.

## 11. WARRANTIES

11.1 AtliQ warrants that the Services shall be performed in a professional manner consistent with generally accepted industry standards and that the Deliverables will materially conform to Schedule A for sixty (60) days after Acceptance.
11.2 EXCEPT AS EXPRESSLY SET OUT IN THIS AGREEMENT, NEITHER PARTY MAKES ANY OTHER WARRANTY, EXPRESS OR IMPLIED.

## 12. LIMITATION OF LIABILITY

12.1 Neither Party shall be liable for indirect, consequential, special or punitive damages or loss of profits.
12.2 Each Party's total liability arising out of this Agreement shall not exceed the total fees paid under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim, except for breach of confidentiality or wilful misconduct.

## 13. INDEMNIFICATION

13.1 AtliQ shall defend and indemnify TravelHub against third-party claims alleging that the Deliverables infringe any intellectual property right.
13.2 TravelHub shall defend and indemnify AtliQ against third-party claims arising from Customer Data or TravelHub's use of the Deliverables in breach of applicable law.

## 14. DATA PROTECTION

14.1 AtliQ shall process personal data only on TravelHub's documented instructions and in compliance with Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 on the Protection of Personal Data and, where applicable, the Saudi Personal Data Protection Law.
14.2 AtliQ shall not transfer Customer Data outside the TravelHub cloud environment without prior written approval.

## 15. GOVERNING LAW AND JURISDICTION

15.1 This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the Emirate of Dubai and the applicable federal laws of the United Arab Emirates.
15.2 The courts of the Emirate of Dubai (onshore Dubai Courts) shall have exclusive jurisdiction over any dispute arising out of or in connection with this Agreement.

## 16. GENERAL

16.1 **Non-solicitation.** During the term and for twelve (12) months thereafter, neither Party shall solicit for employment any employee of the other Party directly involved in the Services.
16.2 **Assignment.** Neither Party may assign this Agreement without the other's prior written consent, except to an Affiliate or successor in a merger.
16.3 **Publicity.** AtliQ may list TravelHub as a customer on its website with TravelHub's prior approval.
16.4 **Entire Agreement.** This Agreement and its Schedules constitute the entire agreement of the Parties.
16.5 **Notices.** Notices to TravelHub shall be sent to Ms. Nadia Rahman, Co-founder; notices to AtliQ shall be sent to its President.

# EXHIBIT D — BUSINESS ASSOCIATE AGREEMENT

**Harrington Health Systems, Inc. — Contract No. HHS-IT-2026-0193, Exhibit D**
**Form: HHS Business Associate Agreement (Rev. 03/2026)**

This Business Associate Agreement (this "**BAA**") is entered into as of the Effective Date of the Master Services Agreement (as defined below) by and between **Harrington Health Systems, Inc.**, a Texas nonprofit corporation with its principal place of business at 6400 Fannin Street, Suite 1800, Houston, Texas 77030, on behalf of itself and its Affiliates that are covered entities ("**Covered Entity**" or "**Harrington**"), and **AtliQ Inc**, a Delaware corporation with its principal place of business at 101 College Road East, Suite 210, Princeton, New Jersey 08540 ("**Business Associate**").

## RECITALS

WHEREAS, Covered Entity and Business Associate are parties to the Master Professional Services Agreement, Contract No. HHS-IT-2026-0193 (together with all Statements of Work and Exhibits thereto, the "**Master Services Agreement**"), under which Business Associate will perform services that involve the creation, receipt, maintenance or transmission of Protected Health Information on behalf of Covered Entity;

WHEREAS, Covered Entity is required by HIPAA to obtain satisfactory assurances that Business Associate will appropriately safeguard Protected Health Information;

NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the mutual promises herein and in the Master Services Agreement, the Parties agree as follows:

## ARTICLE 1 — DEFINITIONS

1.1 "**HIPAA**" means the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act of 1996, the Health Information Technology for Economic and Clinical Health Act (Title XIII of the American Recovery and Reinvestment Act of 2009), and the regulations at 45 C.F.R. Parts 160, 162 and 164, each as amended.
1.2 "**Protected Health Information**" or "**PHI**" has the meaning given at 45 C.F.R. § 160.103, limited to information created, received, maintained or transmitted by Business Associate or any Subcontractor on behalf of Covered Entity, and includes electronic PHI.
1.3 "**Security Incident**" has the meaning given at 45 C.F.R. § 164.304.
1.4 "**Breach**" has the meaning given at 45 C.F.R. § 164.402.
1.5 "**Subcontractor**" means any person or entity, including any Affiliate of Business Associate, to whom Business Associate delegates a function, activity or service under the Master Services Agreement, other than in the capacity of a member of Business Associate's workforce.
1.6 "**Privacy Event**" means any (a) Security Incident; (b) Breach; (c) use or disclosure of PHI not permitted by this BAA; or (d) suspected occurrence of any of the foregoing.
1.7 "**Texas Privacy Law**" means the Texas Medical Records Privacy Act (Tex. Health & Safety Code ch. 181) and Tex. Bus. & Com. Code ch. 521.
1.8 Capitalized terms used but not defined in this BAA have the meanings given in HIPAA or, if not defined there, in the Master Services Agreement.

## ARTICLE 2 — PERMITTED USES AND DISCLOSURES

2.1 Business Associate may use or disclose PHI solely as necessary to perform the Services under the Master Services Agreement, in compliance with this BAA and the minimum necessary standard at 45 C.F.R. § 164.502(b).
2.2 Business Associate may use PHI for its proper management and administration or to carry out its legal responsibilities, and may disclose PHI for such purposes only if Required By Law or if Business Associate obtains reasonable written assurances from the recipient as required by 45 C.F.R. § 164.504(e)(4).
2.3 Business Associate shall not (a) sell PHI; (b) use or disclose PHI for marketing or fundraising; (c) perform Data Aggregation services except as expressly authorized in writing by Covered Entity; or (d) use or disclose PHI in any manner that would violate Subpart E of 45 C.F.R. Part 164 if done by Covered Entity.
2.4 Business Associate shall not de-identify PHI, or use de-identified information derived from PHI for any purpose other than the Services, without Covered Entity's prior written approval.

## ARTICLE 3 — SAFEGUARDS

3.1 Business Associate shall implement administrative, physical and technical safeguards that reasonably and appropriately protect the confidentiality, integrity and availability of electronic PHI, and shall comply with Subpart C of 45 C.F.R. Part 164.
3.2 Business Associate shall comply with the Client Information Security Requirements set forth in Exhibit B to the Master Services Agreement, including encryption of PHI at rest and in transit, multi-factor authentication, and logging and monitoring of all access to PHI.
3.3 Business Associate shall ensure that all members of its workforce with access to PHI have completed HIPAA privacy and security training prior to access and annually thereafter, and shall provide training records upon request.
3.4 Business Associate shall apply sanctions against members of its workforce who fail to comply with its privacy and security policies, consistent with 45 C.F.R. § 164.530(e), and shall promptly revoke access to PHI upon termination or reassignment of any such person.
3.5 Business Associate shall maintain a documented security risk analysis covering all systems used to access PHI in accordance with 45 C.F.R. § 164.308(a)(1)(ii)(A), and shall update it at least annually.

## ARTICLE 4 — LOCATION OF PHI; SUBCONTRACTORS

4.1 **Domestic Performance.** Business Associate shall not, and shall ensure that no Subcontractor shall, access, view, create, receive, maintain, transmit, store or process PHI from or at any location outside the United States, whether directly or by remote access.
4.2 **Subcontractor Requirements.** Business Associate shall not engage any Subcontractor in connection with the Services without Covered Entity's prior written approval of such Subcontractor. Each approved Subcontractor shall be organized under the laws of a State of the United States, and all of its personnel performing Services shall be located in the United States.
4.3 **Flow-Down.** In accordance with 45 C.F.R. §§ 164.502(e)(1)(ii) and 164.308(b)(2), Business Associate shall ensure that each Subcontractor agrees in writing, prior to any access to PHI, to the same restrictions, conditions and requirements that apply to Business Associate under this BAA. Business Associate shall provide a copy of each such agreement to Covered Entity upon request.
4.4 Business Associate shall remain fully responsible for the acts and omissions of its Subcontractors as if they were Business Associate's own.

## ARTICLE 5 — REPORTING OF PRIVACY EVENTS

5.1 **Notice.** Business Associate shall notify Covered Entity's Privacy Officer by telephone and in writing of any Privacy Event within twenty-four (24) hours of discovery. A Privacy Event shall be deemed discovered on the first day on which it is known, or by exercising reasonable diligence would have been known, to any employee, officer, agent or Subcontractor of Business Associate.
5.2 **Content.** Business Associate's notice shall include, to the extent known, the information described at 45 C.F.R. § 164.410(c), and Business Associate shall supplement such notice within five (5) days and thereafter as information becomes available.
5.3 **Unsuccessful Attempts.** Notice is hereby deemed given for unsuccessful Security Incidents, such as pings, port scans and denied log-in attempts, that do not result in unauthorized access, use or disclosure of PHI.
5.4 **Cooperation.** Business Associate shall cooperate fully in Covered Entity's investigation of any Privacy Event and shall not notify any Individual, regulator or media outlet of a Privacy Event without Covered Entity's prior written consent, except as Required By Law.
5.5 **Mitigation.** Business Associate shall promptly mitigate, at its own expense, any harmful effect of a Privacy Event.

## ARTICLE 6 — INDIVIDUAL RIGHTS

6.1 Within five (5) business days of Covered Entity's request, Business Associate shall make PHI maintained in a Designated Record Set available to Covered Entity as necessary to satisfy 45 C.F.R. § 164.524, including in electronic form where requested.
6.2 Within five (5) business days of Covered Entity's request, Business Associate shall incorporate any amendment to PHI in a Designated Record Set as directed by Covered Entity under 45 C.F.R. § 164.526.
6.3 Business Associate shall document disclosures of PHI and provide to Covered Entity, within ten (10) business days of request, the information required for an accounting of disclosures under 45 C.F.R. § 164.528.
6.4 Business Associate shall forward to Covered Entity within three (3) business days any request received directly from an Individual.

## ARTICLE 7 — COMPLIANCE AND AUDIT

7.1 **HHS Access.** Business Associate shall make its internal practices, books and records relating to the use and disclosure of PHI available to the Secretary for purposes of determining Covered Entity's compliance with HIPAA.
7.2 **Covered Entity Audit.** Covered Entity or its designee may inspect and audit Business Associate's and any Subcontractor's facilities, systems, books, records, policies and procedures relating to PHI upon forty-eight (48) hours' notice, at any time during the term of this BAA and for so long as Business Associate retains any PHI. Business Associate shall promptly remediate any deficiency identified.
7.3 **Texas Privacy Law.** Business Associate shall comply with Texas Privacy Law to the extent applicable to Business Associate, including training requirements for employees who handle PHI.
7.4 **Litigation Support.** Business Associate shall make itself and its workforce reasonably available to Covered Entity, at no cost, to testify in any litigation or administrative proceeding against Covered Entity relating to Business Associate's use or disclosure of PHI, except where Business Associate is a named adverse party.

## ARTICLE 8 — INDEMNIFICATION; INSURANCE

8.1 **Indemnification.** Business Associate shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Covered Entity, its Affiliates and their respective trustees, officers, employees and agents from and against any and all Losses arising out of or relating to (a) any Privacy Event involving Business Associate or any Subcontractor; (b) any breach of this BAA by Business Associate or any Subcontractor; or (c) any violation of HIPAA or Texas Privacy Law by Business Associate or any Subcontractor, including without limitation regulatory fines, civil monetary penalties, costs of notification of Individuals, regulators and media, call-center support, credit monitoring and identity theft protection for affected Individuals, forensic investigation, and reasonable attorneys' fees.
8.2 **No Limitation.** The obligations of Business Associate under this Article 8 are not subject to any limitation or exclusion of liability, and shall apply notwithstanding any limitation of liability in the Master Services Agreement.
8.3 **Insurance.** Business Associate shall maintain, throughout the term of this BAA and for three (3) years thereafter, cyber liability and network security and privacy insurance with limits of not less than Five Million U.S. Dollars ($5,000,000) per claim and in the aggregate, covering notification costs, regulatory defense and penalties, and third-party claims arising from Privacy Events, and shall name Covered Entity as an additional insured.

## ARTICLE 9 — OBLIGATIONS OF COVERED ENTITY

9.1 Covered Entity shall notify Business Associate of (a) any limitation in its notice of privacy practices under 45 C.F.R. § 164.520; (b) any change in, or revocation of, an Individual's authorization to use or disclose PHI; and (c) any restriction on the use or disclosure of PHI agreed to by Covered Entity under 45 C.F.R. § 164.522, in each case to the extent it may affect Business Associate's use or disclosure of PHI.
9.2 Covered Entity shall not request Business Associate to use or disclose PHI in any manner that would not be permissible under HIPAA if done by Covered Entity, except as permitted by Section 2.2.
9.3 Covered Entity shall provide PHI to Business Associate only through the secure transfer methods or Client-controlled environments specified in Exhibit B to the Master Services Agreement.

## ARTICLE 10 — OWNERSHIP OF PHI; ELECTRONIC TRANSACTIONS

10.1 As between the Parties, all PHI and all data derived from PHI is and shall remain the sole property of Covered Entity. Business Associate acquires no right, title or interest in PHI by reason of this BAA or the Master Services Agreement.
10.2 To the extent Business Associate conducts any Standard Transaction on behalf of Covered Entity, Business Associate shall comply with 45 C.F.R. Part 162 and shall require any Subcontractor to do the same.

**Agreement Reference: GCHR/IT/MSA/2026/047**

This Master Services Agreement (the "**Agreement**") is made and entered into on the ____ day of __________ 2026 (the "**Effective Date**").

## 1. PARTIES

1.1 **Gulf Crown Hotels & Resorts Co.**, a closed joint stock company incorporated under the laws of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, holding Commercial Registration No. 1010584431, with its head office at King Fahd Road, Al Olaya District, P.O. Box 88214, Riyadh 11662, Kingdom of Saudi Arabia (the "**Company**"); and

1.2 **AtliQ Technologies Pvt Ltd**, a private limited company incorporated under the laws of the Republic of India, bearing CIN U72900MH2019PTC321456, with its registered office at 4th Floor, Baner Business Bay, Pune 411045, Maharashtra, India (the "**Service Provider**").

The Company and the Service Provider are each referred to as a "**Party**" and together as the "**Parties**".

## 2. RECITALS

2.1 WHEREAS the Company owns and operates a portfolio of hotels and resorts within the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia and wishes to modernise its commercial and guest-facing operations in line with its Digital Transformation Programme;

2.2 WHEREAS the Service Provider has represented that it possesses the requisite expertise, qualified personnel and experience in data platforms, analytics and artificial intelligence to design, build and deploy the Platform described herein;

2.3 AND WHEREAS the Company, relying upon the representations of the Service Provider, wishes to engage the Service Provider, and the Service Provider wishes to be engaged, upon the terms and conditions set forth in this Agreement.

NOW, THEREFORE, the Parties, having full legal capacity to contract, have agreed as follows.

## 3. DEFINITIONS

3.1 "**Platform**" means the revenue management and guest analytics platform to be delivered by the Service Provider under this Agreement, as further described in Clause 4 and Schedule 1.
3.2 "**Properties**" means the hotels and resorts owned or operated by the Company and listed in Schedule 2.
3.3 "**Deliverables**" means all software, dashboards, models, documentation, reports and other materials to be provided by the Service Provider under this Agreement.
3.4 "**Milestone**" means each stage of the Services identified in Schedule 3, together with its associated completion date.
3.5 "**Contract Value**" means the total fees payable under this Agreement, being One Hundred and Forty Thousand United States Dollars (USD 140,000).
3.6 "**Business Day**" means any day other than a Friday, Saturday or official public holiday in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia.
3.7 "**Confidential Information**" means all information disclosed by one Party to the other, whether oral, written or electronic, that is designated as confidential or that ought reasonably to be understood as confidential.
3.8 "**Guest Data**" means any personal data relating to guests, members of the Company's loyalty programme, or prospective guests of the Properties.

## 4. SCOPE OF SERVICES

4.1 The Service Provider shall design, develop, test, deploy and support a revenue management and guest analytics platform for the Company's nine (9) Properties located in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, as listed in Schedule 2.
4.2 The Platform shall include, at a minimum, the following components:
   (a) **Revenue Management Module** — demand forecasting at room-type and night level, dynamic rate recommendations, competitor rate ingestion, pickup and pace analysis, and a length-of-stay and overbooking optimisation engine;
   (b) **Guest Analytics Module** — a unified guest profile consolidating data from the Company's property management system, central reservation system, loyalty programme and point-of-sale systems; guest segmentation; lifetime value scoring; and propensity models for upsell and repeat stay;
   (c) **Executive and Property Dashboards** — Arabic and English dashboards for the Chief Commercial Officer, Revenue Managers and General Managers of each Property;
   (d) **Integrations** — integration with the Company's existing property management system, channel manager and CRM at each Property;
   (e) **Training and Handover** — training for up to forty (40) Company personnel across the Properties.
4.3 The Service Provider shall perform the Services in accordance with the specifications set out in Schedule 1, the Milestones set out in Schedule 3, and any reasonable instructions issued by the Company's Project Director.
4.4 The Service Provider shall deploy a dedicated project manager who shall be available during Riyadh business hours and shall attend on-site at the Company's head office as reasonably requested.
4.5 Any change to the scope of Services shall be agreed in writing through a change request signed by authorised representatives of both Parties.

## 5. FEES AND PAYMENT

5.1 In consideration of the Services, the Company shall pay the Service Provider the Contract Value in accordance with the payment schedule in Schedule 3.
5.2 The Service Provider shall submit an invoice upon the Company's written acceptance of each Milestone. Invoices shall be addressed to the Company's Finance Department and shall reference the Agreement Reference number.
5.3 The Company shall pay each undisputed invoice within sixty (60) days from the date of receipt of a valid invoice.
5.4 All fees are exclusive of Value Added Tax. Where the Company is required by law to withhold any tax from payments, the Company shall deduct such tax and provide the Service Provider with the relevant withholding certificate.
5.5 The Company may dispute any invoice in good faith by written notice within fifteen (15) Business Days of receipt, and the Parties shall endeavour to resolve such dispute amicably.
5.6 All payments shall be made in United States Dollars by bank transfer to the account nominated by the Service Provider in writing.

## 6. TERM AND TERMINATION

6.1 This Agreement shall commence on the Effective Date and shall continue for a period of thirty-six (36) months, unless terminated earlier in accordance with this Clause 6.
6.2 Either Party may terminate this Agreement by written notice if the other Party commits a material breach and fails to remedy such breach within thirty (30) days of receiving written notice thereof.
6.3 The Company may terminate this Agreement for convenience upon sixty (60) days' written notice, in which event the Company shall pay for all Services performed and accepted up to the date of termination.
6.4 Either Party may terminate this Agreement immediately if the other Party becomes insolvent, enters into liquidation or makes any arrangement with its creditors.
6.5 Upon termination, the Service Provider shall deliver to the Company all Deliverables and work in progress, and shall provide reasonable transition assistance for a period of up to sixty (60) days.

## 7. CONFIDENTIALITY

7.1 Each Party shall keep confidential all Confidential Information of the other Party and shall not disclose it to any third party without prior written consent, save to its employees, advisers and subcontractors who need to know it for the purposes of this Agreement and who are bound by obligations of confidentiality no less stringent than those herein.
7.2 The obligations in this Clause 7 shall not apply to information which is or becomes publicly available other than through breach of this Agreement, was lawfully in the receiving Party's possession prior to disclosure, or is required to be disclosed by law or by a competent authority.
7.3 The obligations in this Clause 7 shall survive for a period of five (5) years following the expiry or termination of this Agreement.

## 8. INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY

8.1 All Deliverables specifically created for the Company under this Agreement shall, upon payment in full, become the property of the Company.
8.2 The Service Provider shall retain ownership of its pre-existing tools, methodologies and know-how ("**Background IP**"). To the extent any Background IP is incorporated into the Deliverables, the Service Provider grants the Company a non-exclusive, perpetual, royalty-free licence to use such Background IP solely as part of the Deliverables for the Company's internal business purposes.
8.3 The Company shall retain all rights in its data, including Guest Data, and in any materials provided by the Company to the Service Provider.

## 9. WARRANTIES

9.1 The Service Provider warrants that:
   (a) the Services shall be performed with reasonable skill, care and diligence and in accordance with good industry practice;
   (b) the Deliverables shall conform in all material respects to the specifications in Schedule 1 for a period of ninety (90) days following acceptance;
   (c) it has the full right, power and authority to enter into and perform this Agreement; and
   (d) it is not bound by any agreement or restriction which would prevent or restrict it from performing the Services for the Company.
9.2 The Service Provider shall, at its own cost, remedy any defect notified by the Company during the warranty period.

## 10. LIMITATION OF LIABILITY

10.1 Neither Party shall be liable to the other for any indirect, special or consequential loss, or loss of profits, arising out of or in connection with this Agreement.
10.2 Save in respect of liability arising from fraud, wilful misconduct, breach of Clause 7 (Confidentiality) or Clause 13 (Data Protection), each Party's aggregate liability under this Agreement shall not exceed the Contract Value.

## 11. INDEMNITY

11.1 The Service Provider shall indemnify the Company against all losses, claims and expenses arising from any claim by a third party that the Deliverables infringe the intellectual property rights of such third party.
11.2 The Company shall indemnify the Service Provider against claims arising from the Service Provider's use, in accordance with this Agreement, of materials supplied by the Company.

## 12. DELAY PENALTIES

12.1 Time shall be of the essence in respect of the Milestone dates set out in Schedule 3.
12.2 Should the Service Provider fail to achieve any Milestone by its scheduled completion date, the Service Provider shall pay to the Company, by way of liquidated damages and not as a penalty, an amount equal to one percent (1%) of the Contract Value for each week or part thereof of delay.
12.3 The aggregate liquidated damages payable under this Clause 12 shall not exceed ten percent (10%) of the Contract Value.
12.4 The Company may deduct any liquidated damages due from any amount payable to the Service Provider under this Agreement.
12.5 The Service Provider shall not be liable for delay to the extent such delay is caused by a Force Majeure Event as defined in Clause 15.

## 13. DATA PROTECTION

13.1 The Service Provider shall process Guest Data only on the documented instructions of the Company and in compliance with the Personal Data Protection Law issued by Royal Decree No. M/19 and its Implementing Regulations, and any other applicable law in the Kingdom.
13.2 Guest Data shall be hosted within the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia unless the Company provides prior written approval for any transfer outside the Kingdom.
13.3 The Service Provider shall implement appropriate technical and organisational measures to protect Guest Data and shall notify the Company of any personal data breach within seventy-two (72) hours of becoming aware of it.

## 14. GOVERNING LAW AND DISPUTE RESOLUTION

14.1 This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws and regulations in force in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia.
14.2 The Parties shall seek to resolve any dispute arising out of or in connection with this Agreement amicably through negotiation between senior executives within thirty (30) days.
14.3 Failing amicable resolution, the dispute shall be referred to the competent courts in the City of Riyadh, Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, which shall have exclusive jurisdiction.

## 15. GENERAL PROVISIONS

15.1 **Force Majeure.** Neither Party shall be liable for failure to perform its obligations where such failure results from events beyond its reasonable control, including acts of God, war, epidemic or governmental action ("**Force Majeure Event**").
15.2 **Assignment.** The Service Provider shall not assign or subcontract any of its obligations without the prior written consent of the Company.
15.3 **Language.** This Agreement is executed in English and Arabic. In the event of any inconsistency, the Arabic text shall prevail.
15.4 **Notices.** All notices shall be in writing and delivered by hand, courier or email to the addresses set out in Clause 1, marked for the attention of the Company's Chief Technology Officer (Mr. Faisal Al-Otaibi) and the Service Provider's Chief Executive Officer respectively.
15.5 **Entire Agreement.** This Agreement, together with its Schedules, constitutes the entire agreement between the Parties and supersedes all prior negotiations and understandings.
15.6 **Amendment.** No amendment shall be effective unless in writing and signed by both Parties.
15.7 **Counterparts.** This Agreement may be executed in counterparts, each of which shall be deemed an original.

   (a) migration of Lakeshore's legacy on-premises SQL Server data warehouse to a cloud lakehouse;
   (b) build of automated ingestion pipelines for point-of-sale, loyalty, inventory and e-commerce order data from all stores;
   (c) a certified semantic layer for sales, margin, shrink and promotions; and

## 13. GOVERNING LAW AND DISPUTE RESOLUTION

## 14. GENERAL

3.2 "**Properties**" means the twelve (12) hotels listed in Annexure B.
3.3 "**Deliverables**" means the solution, dashboards, models, reports and documentation delivered by AtliQ under this Agreement.
3.4 "**Milestone Fee**" means the fee attributable to a Milestone as set out in Annexure C.
3.5 "**Client Data**" means all review data, survey responses, booking references and other data made available by BlueOrchid, including any personal data contained therein.
3.6 "**Pre-existing IP**" means any software, tools, libraries, frameworks, methodologies and know-how owned or developed by a Party prior to or independently of this Agreement.

## 4. SCOPE OF SERVICES

4.1 AtliQ shall deliver a guest review analytics solution for all twelve (12) Properties listed in Annexure B, comprising:
   (a) automated ingestion of guest reviews from up to six (6) online sources and BlueOrchid's post-stay survey tool;
   (b) multilingual sentiment and aspect analysis (English, Hindi, Arabic) covering room, cleanliness, F&B, service, location and value;
   (c) property-level and portfolio-level dashboards in Power BI for General Managers, the Guest Experience team and senior management;
   (d) a weekly automated "Voice of Guest" summary for each Property; and
   (e) an alerting mechanism flagging recurring negative themes for the relevant Property's General Manager.
4.2 The Pilot shall run for a period of sixteen (16) weeks from the Effective Date, comprising a twelve (12) week build and rollout phase and a four (4) week evaluation phase.
4.3 BlueOrchid shall nominate a single point of contact (initially Ms. Farah Sayed, Director – Guest Experience) and shall provide timely access to data sources, systems and personnel reasonably required by AtliQ.
4.4 Any change in scope shall be documented through a written change request agreed by both Parties.

## 5. FEES AND PAYMENT

5.1 The total fee for the Pilot is USD 38,000 (United States Dollars Thirty-Eight Thousand only), payable in accordance with the Milestones in Annexure C.
5.2 AtliQ shall raise an invoice on completion of each Milestone. BlueOrchid shall pay each undisputed invoice within thirty (30) days of receipt.
5.3 All amounts are exclusive of GST, which shall be charged at the applicable rate. BlueOrchid may deduct TDS as required under the Income-tax Act, 1961, and shall furnish TDS certificates within the statutory timelines.
5.4 Any disputed portion of an invoice shall be notified within ten (10) days of receipt; the undisputed portion shall be paid in accordance with Clause 5.2.

## 6. TERM AND TERMINATION

6.1 This Agreement shall commence on the Effective Date and remain in force until completion of the Pilot, unless terminated earlier.
6.2 Either Party may terminate this Agreement for material breach not remedied within thirty (30) days of written notice.
6.3 BlueOrchid may terminate this Agreement for convenience on thirty (30) days' written notice, subject to payment for all work performed up to the effective date of termination, including a pro-rata amount for any Milestone in progress.
6.4 Clauses 7, 8, 10, 11, 13 and 14 shall survive termination or expiry.

## 7. CONFIDENTIALITY

7.1 Each Party shall hold the other Party's confidential information in strict confidence, use it only for the purposes of this Agreement, and disclose it only to its employees and professional advisers on a need-to-know basis.
7.2 These obligations shall not apply to information that is public, already known to the recipient, independently developed, or required to be disclosed by law.
7.3 The obligations in this Clause shall continue for three (3) years after termination or expiry of this Agreement.

## 8. INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY

8.1 Upon payment in full, BlueOrchid shall own the dashboards, reports and configurations created specifically for BlueOrchid under this Agreement.
8.2 Each Party retains all rights in its Pre-existing IP. AtliQ grants BlueOrchid a non-exclusive, non-transferable, royalty-free licence to use AtliQ's Pre-existing IP to the extent incorporated in the Deliverables, solely for BlueOrchid's internal business purposes.
8.3 BlueOrchid retains all rights in Client Data.

## 9. WARRANTIES

9.1 AtliQ warrants that the Services shall be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner by suitably qualified personnel.
9.2 AtliQ shall correct any material non-conformity in the Deliverables notified within thirty (30) days after completion of the Pilot.
9.3 Each Party warrants that it has full power and authority to enter into this Agreement.

## 10. LIMITATION OF LIABILITY

10.1 Neither Party shall be liable for any indirect, incidental, special or consequential damages, including loss of profit, revenue or goodwill.
10.2 Except for breach of confidentiality, fraud or wilful misconduct, each Party's total aggregate liability under this Agreement shall not exceed the total fees paid or payable under this Agreement.

## 11. INDEMNITY

11.1 Each Party (the "Indemnifying Party") shall indemnify the other against third-party claims to the extent arising from the Indemnifying Party's breach of this Agreement, negligence or wilful misconduct.
11.2 AtliQ shall indemnify BlueOrchid against third-party claims that the Deliverables infringe any intellectual property right, save where such claim arises from Client Data or modifications made by BlueOrchid.

## 12. DELAY

12.1 If AtliQ fails to complete a Milestone by its scheduled date for reasons solely attributable to AtliQ, BlueOrchid shall be entitled to liquidated damages of 0.5% of the relevant Milestone Fee for each complete week of delay, subject to a maximum of 5% of that Milestone Fee.
12.2 No liquidated damages shall be payable for any delay caused by BlueOrchid, its vendors, or a force majeure event.
12.3 Liquidated damages under this Clause shall be BlueOrchid's sole and exclusive remedy for delay.

## 13. DATA PROTECTION

13.1 AtliQ shall process personal data contained in Client Data only for the purposes of the Pilot and in accordance with the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 and any other applicable data protection law, including the laws applicable to Properties located outside India.
13.2 AtliQ shall implement reasonable security safeguards and shall notify BlueOrchid without undue delay of any personal data breach.
13.3 On completion or termination of the Pilot, AtliQ shall return or delete Client Data as instructed by BlueOrchid.

## 14. GOVERNING LAW AND DISPUTE RESOLUTION

14.1 This Agreement shall be governed by the laws of India.
14.2 Any dispute shall first be referred to senior management of both Parties for amicable settlement within thirty (30) days.
14.3 Failing settlement, the dispute shall be finally resolved by arbitration under the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, by a sole arbitrator mutually appointed. The seat and venue of arbitration shall be Mumbai and the language shall be English.
14.4 Subject to the above, the courts at Mumbai shall have exclusive jurisdiction.

## 15. GENERAL

15.1 **Force Majeure.** Neither Party shall be liable for delay or failure caused by events beyond its reasonable control.
15.2 **Assignment.** Neither Party may assign this Agreement without the prior written consent of the other, not to be unreasonably withheld.
15.3 **Independent Contractors.** The Parties are independent contractors; nothing herein creates a partnership or agency.
15.4 **Notices.** Notices shall be in writing to the addresses above, marked to the attention of Ms. Farah Sayed (BlueOrchid) and the Chief Executive Officer (AtliQ).
15.5 **Entire Agreement.** This Agreement, with its Annexures, is the entire agreement between the Parties regarding the Pilot.
15.6 **Future Engagement.** Upon successful completion of the Pilot, the Parties may enter into a master services agreement for a full-scale rollout on terms to be mutually agreed.

# SERVICES AGREEMENT
## (Dienstleistungs- und Werkvertrag — English version)

**Contract No. RWA-2026-014**

between

**Rheinwerk Analytics GmbH**, Leopoldstraße 184, 80804 München, Germany, registered in the commercial register of the Local Court (Amtsgericht) of Munich under HRB 241873, VAT ID DE318442907, represented by its Managing Director (Geschäftsführer), Mr. Stefan Brandt

and

— Client and Supplier each a "**Party**", together the "**Parties**" —

## Preamble

Client provides industrial analytics and predictive maintenance software to mid-sized manufacturing companies in the DACH region. Client intends to replace the batch-based data ingestion layer of its "Rheinwerk Insight" platform with a scalable, near-real-time data pipeline architecture. Supplier has experience in the design and implementation of cloud data pipelines. The Parties therefore agree as follows.

## § 1 Definitions

1.1 "**Platform**" means Client's Rheinwerk Insight software-as-a-service platform.
1.2 "**Work Results**" means all results created by Supplier for Client under this Agreement, including source code, configurations, pipeline definitions, documentation and test cases.
1.3 "**Milestone**" means a defined stage of the project as set out in Annex 1.
1.4 "**Milestone Fee**" means the remuneration allocated to a Milestone in Annex 2.
1.5 "**Client Data**" means all data made available by Client or its customers, including sensor, machine and maintenance data and any personal data contained therein.
1.6 "**GDPR**" means Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (General Data Protection Regulation).

## § 2 Subject Matter and Scope of Services

2.1 Supplier shall design, implement and hand over a new data ingestion and processing layer for the Platform, comprising in particular:
   (a) streaming ingestion of machine sensor data (OPC UA / MQTT) from Client's customers' plants into Client's EU cloud environment;
   (b) a medallion-architecture data lakehouse (raw, cleansed, curated layers) with data quality checks;
   (c) migration of 22 existing batch jobs to the new pipeline framework;
   (d) orchestration, monitoring and alerting; and
   (e) documentation and a two-week knowledge transfer to Client's platform engineering team.
2.2 The detailed specification is set out in Annex 1 (Leistungsbeschreibung / Statement of Work).
2.3 Supplier shall perform the services with its own personnel, primarily remotely from India. Supplier personnel shall attend on-site workshops in Munich at the start of the project and for the knowledge transfer.
2.4 Changes to the scope of services require a written change request agreed by both Parties (§ 12.3).

## § 3 Client's Cooperation Duties

3.1 Client shall provide Supplier with timely access to the required cloud environments, source systems, test data and contact persons.
3.2 Client shall nominate a project lead with decision-making authority.
3.3 Delays caused by Client's failure to fulfil its cooperation duties shall extend the relevant deadlines accordingly.

## § 4 Remuneration and Payment

4.1 The total fixed remuneration for the services under this Agreement is **EUR 88,000** (eighty-eight thousand euros) net, payable in accordance with the Milestones in Annex 2.
4.2 Supplier shall invoice each Milestone Fee after acceptance of the relevant Milestone. Invoices are payable within thirty (30) days of receipt without deduction.
4.3 All amounts are net. Where the reverse-charge procedure under § 13b UStG applies, the invoice shall so indicate. Withholding taxes, if any, shall be handled in accordance with the applicable double taxation agreement between Germany and India, and Client shall provide the relevant certificates.
4.4 Travel expenses for on-site workshops shall be reimbursed at cost up to a maximum of EUR 6,000 in total, subject to prior approval.

## § 5 Acceptance (Abnahme)

5.1 Each Milestone requiring acceptance shall be submitted to Client for acceptance testing. Client shall declare acceptance within ten (10) working days of submission if the Work Results conform in all material respects to Annex 1.
5.2 Minor defects shall not entitle Client to refuse acceptance; they shall be recorded in the acceptance protocol and remedied within a reasonable period.
5.3 If Client fails to declare acceptance or to specify material defects within the period set out in § 5.1, acceptance shall be deemed to have been granted.

## § 6 Supplier Tools and Rights of Use

6.1 Supplier shall deliver the services using its proprietary data-pipeline accelerator "**PipeKit**", comprising reusable ingestion connectors, transformation templates, data quality rule libraries and orchestration modules. PipeKit shall be incorporated into the Work Results to reduce implementation time and cost.
6.2 Supplier hereby grants Client a perpetual, irrevocable, non-exclusive, worldwide, royalty-free right to use, reproduce, modify and operate PipeKit as incorporated in the Work Results, for the purposes of operating, maintaining and further developing the Platform, including for the benefit of Client's customers. Client may sub-license this right to its affiliated companies and to service providers acting on its behalf.
6.3 Supplier warrants that it is the sole owner of all intellectual property rights in PipeKit, that it is entitled to grant the rights set out in § 6.2, and that PipeKit and its use under this Agreement do not infringe any rights of third parties.
6.4 Supplier shall indemnify Client against all third-party claims arising from any breach of the warranty in § 6.3, in accordance with § 10.
6.5 Except for PipeKit, Client shall acquire the exclusive, perpetual, transferable and unrestricted right of use in all Work Results created specifically for Client, upon full payment of the relevant Milestone Fee.
6.6 Open-source components may be used only with Client's prior approval and subject to their respective licence terms, which Supplier shall list in the documentation.

## § 7 Warranty for Defects

7.1 Supplier warrants that the Work Results conform to the specification in Annex 1 at the time of acceptance.
7.2 The warranty period is twelve (12) months from acceptance.
7.3 Supplier shall remedy defects by rectification or new delivery at its option. If remedy fails twice, Client may reduce the remuneration for the affected Milestone or withdraw from the affected part of the Agreement.

## § 8 Delay

8.1 Deadlines for the Milestones are set out in Annex 2.
8.2 If Supplier is in default with a Milestone for reasons for which it is responsible, Client may claim a contractual penalty (Vertragsstrafe) of 0.5% of the Milestone Fee of the affected Milestone for each full week of delay, up to a maximum of 5% of that Milestone Fee.
8.3 No penalty shall be payable to the extent the delay is caused by Client, including by failure to fulfil its cooperation duties under § 3, or by force majeure.
8.4 The contractual penalty shall be credited against any claim for damages for the same delay.

## § 9 Liability

9.1 The Parties shall be liable without limitation for damage caused intentionally or by gross negligence, for injury to life, body or health, and under the Product Liability Act (Produkthaftungsgesetz).
9.2 In the case of slightly negligent breach of a material contractual obligation (Kardinalpflicht), liability shall be limited to the foreseeable damage typical for this type of contract, and in any event to the total remuneration under this Agreement.
9.3 Otherwise, liability for slight negligence is excluded.
9.4 Liability for loss of data is limited to the cost of restoration that would have been incurred had Client carried out regular data backups in line with good practice.

## § 10 Indemnification

10.1 Each Party shall indemnify the other against third-party claims resulting from its culpable breach of this Agreement.
10.2 The indemnified Party shall notify the indemnifying Party without delay of any claim, shall not acknowledge any claim without consent, and shall leave the conduct of the defence to the indemnifying Party.

## § 11 Confidentiality

11.1 The Parties shall keep confidential all business and trade secrets of the other Party that come to their knowledge in connection with this Agreement, and shall use them only for the performance of this Agreement.
11.2 This obligation does not apply to information that is publicly known, was already known to the receiving Party, or is required to be disclosed by law or official order.
11.3 The confidentiality obligation shall continue for five (5) years after termination of this Agreement.

## § 12 Term, Termination, Changes

12.1 This Agreement enters into force upon signature by both Parties and ends upon acceptance of the final Milestone and expiry of the warranty period.
12.2 The right of either Party to terminate for good cause (aus wichtigem Grund) remains unaffected. Good cause exists in particular if the other Party materially breaches its obligations and fails to remedy the breach within thirty (30) days of written notice. Upon termination by Client for convenience (§ 648 BGB), Supplier shall be entitled to the agreed remuneration for services rendered plus compensation for committed costs.
12.3 Change requests shall be submitted in writing. Supplier shall assess the impact on effort, schedule and remuneration within five (5) working days. Changes become binding only when agreed in writing.

## § 13 Data Protection

13.1 To the extent Supplier processes personal data on behalf of Client, the Parties shall conclude the Data Processing Agreement pursuant to Art. 28 GDPR attached as **Annex 3**, which forms an integral part of this Agreement.
13.2 Transfers of personal data to India shall be based on the EU Standard Contractual Clauses (Module 2, Controller-to-Processor) incorporated in Annex 3, supplemented by the technical and organisational measures described therein.
13.3 Supplier shall ensure that its personnel are bound to confidentiality and data secrecy and receive appropriate data protection training.

## § 14 Governing Law and Place of Jurisdiction

14.1 This Agreement shall be governed by the laws of the Federal Republic of Germany, excluding the UN Convention on Contracts for the International Sale of Goods (CISG).
14.2 The exclusive place of jurisdiction for all disputes arising out of or in connection with this Agreement shall be Munich, Germany.

## § 15 Final Provisions

15.1 Amendments and supplements to this Agreement, including this written form clause, must be made in writing. Text form (e-mail) is sufficient for change requests under § 12.3.
15.2 Should any provision of this Agreement be or become invalid, the validity of the remaining provisions shall not be affected. The Parties shall replace the invalid provision with a valid provision that comes closest to the economic purpose of the invalid provision.
15.3 Supplier may subcontract parts of the services only with Client's prior written consent.
15.4 In the event of discrepancies between this English version and any German translation, the English version shall prevail.

# STRATEGIC PARTNERSHIP AGREEMENT

**Datavane, Inc. — Global Partner Program**
**Agreement No. DV-GPP-2026-0417 | Form: Datavane SPA (Implementation & Referral Partner) v4.2**

This Strategic Partnership Agreement (together with its Schedules, this "**Agreement**") is entered into as of the date of the last signature below (the "**Effective Date**") by and between:

**Datavane, Inc.**, a Delaware corporation with its principal place of business at 575 Market Street, Suite 2200, San Francisco, California 94105, USA ("**Datavane**"); and

**AtliQ Technologies Pvt Ltd**, a private limited company incorporated under the laws of India, CIN U72900MH2019PTC321456, having its registered office at 4th Floor, Baner Business Bay, Pune 411045, Maharashtra, India ("**Partner**").

Datavane and Partner are each a "**Party**" and together the "**Parties**."

## RECITALS

A. Datavane develops and offers the Datavane Lakehouse Platform, a cloud-native lakehouse and unified analytics platform offered on a subscription basis.

B. Partner provides data engineering, analytics, AI/ML and business intelligence services to enterprise customers.

C. Datavane wishes to appoint Partner as a non-exclusive implementation and referral partner for the Datavane Platform in the Territory, and Partner wishes to accept such appointment, on the terms of this Agreement.

## 1. DEFINITIONS

1.1 "**Affiliate**" means any entity that directly or indirectly controls, is controlled by, or is under common control with a Party, where "control" means ownership of more than fifty percent (50%) of the voting interests of an entity.
1.2 "**Datavane Platform**" or "**Platform**" means Datavane's lakehouse, data warehouse, streaming, governance and analytics software offered as a service, including all updates, modules and add-ons made generally available by Datavane.
1.3 "**Customer**" means any person or entity that purchases or evaluates a subscription to the Platform.
1.4 "**Prospect**" means any person or entity that Partner identifies, introduces, registers or refers to Datavane, or with which Partner engages in any discussion regarding the Platform, whether or not such person or entity was an existing client of Partner prior to the Effective Date.
1.5 "**Datavane Account**" means (a) each Customer, (b) each Prospect registered by Partner through the Partner Portal, and (c) each Prospect introduced to Datavane by Partner in any manner, together with such entity's Affiliates.
1.6 "**Joint Deal**" means any transaction under which a Datavane Account purchases a Platform subscription together with implementation, migration, managed or consulting services delivered in whole or in part by Partner.
1.7 "**Joint Deal Revenue**" means all amounts invoiced to a Datavane Account in respect of a Joint Deal, including Platform subscription fees and Partner Services fees, net of taxes.
1.8 "**Partner Services**" means implementation, migration, integration, managed and consulting services relating to the Platform performed by Partner for Datavane Accounts.
1.9 "**Partner Portal**" means Datavane's online partner relationship management system.
1.10 "**Territory**" means the Republic of India; the member states of the Gulf Cooperation Council (United Arab Emirates, Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, State of Qatar, State of Kuwait, Kingdom of Bahrain and Sultanate of Oman); and Europe (the member states of the European Union and the European Economic Area, the United Kingdom and Switzerland).
1.11 "**Marks**" means a Party's trademarks, trade names, service marks and logos.
1.12 "**Losses**" means any and all losses, damages, liabilities, deficiencies, claims, actions, judgments, settlements, interest, awards, penalties, fines, costs or expenses of whatever kind, including reasonable attorneys' fees.

## 2. APPOINTMENT

2.1 **Appointment.** Subject to the terms of this Agreement, Datavane appoints Partner, and Partner accepts appointment, as a non-exclusive "Datavane Premier Implementation Partner" for the Territory.
2.2 **Scope of Activities.** Partner shall (a) actively promote the Platform to Prospects in the Territory; (b) register all Prospects in the Partner Portal within five (5) business days of first substantive contact; (c) deliver Partner Services to Datavane Accounts in accordance with Datavane's published implementation methodology; and (d) participate in joint marketing activities as agreed in the annual joint business plan.
2.3 **Non-Exclusivity.** Datavane may appoint other partners, resellers and service providers in the Territory and may sell directly to any Customer or Prospect, including Prospects registered by Partner.
2.4 **Affiliates.** Partner may perform Partner Services through its Affiliates, provided that Partner shall remain responsible for each Affiliate's compliance with this Agreement, and all obligations of Partner hereunder shall bind Partner's Affiliates.
2.5 **Deal Registration.** A Prospect registration is valid for ninety (90) days. Datavane may accept or reject any registration in its sole discretion. Acceptance of a registration does not guarantee that Partner will be engaged for any Joint Deal.

## 3. PARTNER OBLIGATIONS

3.1 **Certified Personnel.** Partner shall maintain at least six (6) Datavane Certified Engineers and one (1) Datavane Certified Architect throughout the Term, and shall ensure that all Partner Services are led by a Datavane Certified Architect.
3.2 **Pipeline Commitment.** Partner shall use commercially reasonable efforts to register not fewer than twelve (12) qualified Prospects in each contract year.
3.3 **Conduct.** Partner shall not make any representation, warranty or commitment regarding the Platform other than as set out in Datavane's then-current published documentation.
3.4 **Compliance.** Partner shall comply with Datavane's Partner Code of Conduct, applicable anti-corruption laws (including the U.S. Foreign Corrupt Practices Act and the UK Bribery Act 2010) and applicable export control and sanctions laws.
3.5 **Reporting.** Partner shall provide Datavane with a monthly pipeline report and a quarterly business review in the format reasonably specified by Datavane.

## 4. DATAVANE OBLIGATIONS

4.1 Datavane shall provide Partner with (a) access to the Partner Portal; (b) up to ten (10) free certification vouchers per contract year; (c) a non-production Platform sandbox environment; and (d) a named partner manager.
4.2 Datavane may, in its discretion, provide Partner with pre-sales support, marketing development funds and co-marketing materials.

## 5. DATAVANE ACCOUNTS

5.1 **Ownership of Relationship.** Partner acknowledges that each Datavane Account is a customer relationship of Datavane. All information relating to Datavane Accounts, including contact details, requirements, usage data and pricing, shall be Datavane's Confidential Information.
5.2 **Registration of Existing Clients.** Where Partner proposes the Platform to an existing client of Partner, Partner shall register such client in the Partner Portal as a Prospect, whereupon such client shall become a Datavane Account.
5.3 **Non-Solicitation of Datavane Accounts.** During the Term and for a period of twenty-four (24) months following expiration or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Partner shall not, and shall cause its Affiliates not to, directly or indirectly solicit, market to, or provide any implementation, migration, managed or consulting services to any Datavane Account in connection with any cloud data warehouse, lakehouse, data platform or analytics platform other than the Datavane Platform.
5.4 **Transition of Accounts.** Upon expiration or termination, Partner shall, at Datavane's request, provide reasonable cooperation in transitioning all Partner Services for Datavane Accounts to Datavane or to a partner designated by Datavane.

## 6. FEES AND REVENUE SHARE

6.1 **Joint Deal Revenue Share.** Joint Deal Revenue shall be shared between the Parties in the proportion of eighty percent (80%) to Datavane and twenty percent (20%) to Partner, irrespective of whether Platform subscription fees or Partner Services fees are the larger component of such Joint Deal.
6.2 **Billing.** Datavane shall invoice Datavane Accounts for all Joint Deal Revenue, unless Datavane agrees in writing that Partner may invoice Partner Services directly, in which case Partner shall remit Datavane's share within thirty (30) days of Partner's invoice date.
6.3 **Payment to Partner.** Datavane shall pay Partner's share of Joint Deal Revenue within sixty (60) days after the end of the calendar quarter in which Datavane receives payment from the relevant Datavane Account.
6.4 **Referral Fee.** For Prospects referred by Partner that purchase a Platform subscription without Partner Services, Datavane shall pay Partner a referral fee of eight percent (8%) of first-year net subscription fees actually received by Datavane.
6.5 **Taxes.** Each Party shall bear its own taxes. Any withholding tax required by law shall be deducted from payments and the paying Party shall provide the relevant withholding certificate.
6.6 **Currency.** All amounts under this Agreement are in United States Dollars.
6.7 **Audit.** Datavane may, upon fifteen (15) days' notice, audit Partner's records relating to Joint Deals and Partner Services.

## 7. TERM AND TERMINATION

7.1 **Term.** This Agreement commences on the Effective Date and continues for an initial term of three (3) years, and thereafter renews automatically for successive one (1) year periods unless Datavane gives notice of non-renewal at least thirty (30) days before the end of the then-current term (the "**Term**").
7.2 **Termination for Convenience by Datavane.** Datavane may terminate this Agreement at any time, for any reason or no reason, upon fifteen (15) days' written notice to Partner.
7.3 **No Termination for Convenience by Partner.** Partner acknowledges the investment made by Datavane in enabling Partner and agrees that Partner may not terminate this Agreement for convenience during the initial term.
7.4 **Termination for Cause.** Either Party may terminate this Agreement upon written notice if the other Party materially breaches this Agreement and fails to cure such breach within thirty (30) days after written notice. Datavane may terminate immediately upon written notice if Partner breaches Section 3.3, 3.4 or 5.
7.5 **Effect of Termination.** Upon expiration or termination: (a) all rights granted to Partner shall terminate; (b) Partner shall cease use of Datavane's Marks and return or destroy Datavane's Confidential Information; (c) no revenue share or referral fee shall be payable in respect of any Joint Deal or referral not fully paid by the relevant Datavane Account before the effective date of termination; and (d) Sections 1, 5.1, 5.3, 5.4, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12 and 13 shall survive.

## 8. INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY AND MARKS

8.1 Datavane retains all right, title and interest in the Platform, its documentation, the Partner Portal and all related intellectual property.
