# STATEMENT OF WORK No. 2

**Distributor Portal v2 and Sales Performance Dashboard**

**SOW Reference:** ATQ-SUN-SOW-02
**Under:** Master Services Agreement between Sunrise Foods Pvt Ltd and AtliQ Technologies Pvt Ltd dated 18 April 2025 (the "**MSA**")

## 1. Parties

This Statement of Work ("**SOW**") is entered into on ____________ 2026 between **Sunrise Foods Pvt Ltd**, having its registered office at Sunrise House, NH 66 Bypass, Edappally, Kochi 682024, Kerala, India ("**Client**"), and **AtliQ Technologies Pvt Ltd**, having its registered office at 4th Floor, Baner Business Bay, Pune 411045, Maharashtra, India, GSTIN 27AAKCA4821F1Z3 ("**AtliQ**").

## 2. Relationship to the MSA

2.1 This SOW is issued under and governed by the MSA. Capitalised terms not defined here have the meanings given in the MSA.
2.2 In the event of any conflict between this SOW and the MSA, the MSA shall prevail, except where this SOW expressly states otherwise for the purposes of this SOW only.

## 3. Background

Under SOW No. 1, AtliQ delivered version 1 of the Sunrise distributor portal, which is used by approximately 140 distributors across Kerala, Tamil Nadu and Karnataka for order placement and scheme tracking. The Client now wishes to extend the portal and give its sales leadership a consolidated view of secondary sales performance.

## 4. Scope of Services

4.1 **Distributor Portal v2**
   (a) Credit-limit visibility and online payment reconciliation for distributors;
   (b) Scheme and promotion eligibility calculator;
   (c) Mobile-responsive redesign and Malayalam / Tamil language support;
   (d) Integration with the Client's ERP for real-time stock availability.

4.2 **Sales Performance Dashboard**
   (a) Power BI dashboard covering primary and secondary sales by region, distributor, SKU and salesperson;
   (b) Target-vs-actual tracking and scheme ROI analysis;
   (c) Weekly automated email summaries to regional sales managers.

4.3 **Out of scope:** retailer-level (tertiary) sales tracking, changes to the Client's ERP, and hosting costs (borne directly by the Client).

## 5. Milestones and Fees

| Milestone | Deliverable | Target Date | Milestone Fee (USD) |
|---|---|---|---|
| M1 | Requirements sign-off and UX designs | Start + 3 weeks | 6,750 |
| M2 | Portal v2 features (4.1 a–b) in UAT | Start + 9 weeks | 13,500 |
| M3 | Portal v2 go-live (4.1 c–d) | Start + 13 weeks | 11,250 |
| M4 | Sales Performance Dashboard live; handover | Start + 16 weeks | 13,500 |
| | **Total** | | **45,000** |

5.1 Fees are exclusive of GST, which shall be charged at the applicable rate.
5.2 AtliQ shall invoice each Milestone Fee on acceptance of the relevant Milestone. The Client shall pay within thirty (30) days of receipt of invoice, as per the MSA.

## 6. Acceptance

6.1 The Client shall review each Deliverable within seven (7) working days of delivery and either confirm acceptance or share a consolidated list of defects against the agreed requirements.
6.2 A Deliverable shall be deemed accepted if no response is received within that period or if it is used in production.

## 7. Client Responsibilities

7.1 Provide ERP API access and test credentials within two (2) weeks of the start date.
7.2 Nominate Ms. Meera Pillai as the single point of contact with authority to approve designs and accept Deliverables.
7.3 Arrange distributor representatives for UAT sessions.

## 8. Penalty for Delay

8.1 If AtliQ fails to achieve a Milestone by its Target Date for reasons attributable to AtliQ, the Client shall be entitled to a service credit equal to 0.5% (half a percent) of the Milestone Fee of the delayed Milestone for each complete week of delay.
8.2 The total service credit for any Milestone shall not exceed 5% of that Milestone Fee.
8.3 No service credit shall apply to any delay caused by the Client, including delays in providing ERP access, approvals or UAT participation under Section 7, or by a force majeure event under the MSA.
8.4 Service credits shall be adjusted against the next invoice and shall be the Client's sole remedy for delay.

## 9. Project Team

Any change to scope, timeline or fees shall be handled through the change request process in the MSA.

## 11. Term

This SOW commences on the date of signature and remains in force until acceptance of Milestone M4 and expiry of the warranty period under the MSA, unless terminated earlier in accordance with the MSA.

All other terms, including confidentiality, intellectual property, warranties, limitation of liability, data protection, governing law (laws of India) and dispute resolution (arbitration seated in Pune), are as set out in the MSA.

## RECITALS

## 1. DEFINITIONS

   (a) is or becomes generally available to the public other than through a breach by the Recipient or its Representatives;
   (b) was in the lawful possession of the Recipient prior to disclosure, free of any obligation of confidence; or
   (c) is lawfully received by the Recipient from a third party not under any obligation of confidence to the Company.

3.2 If the Recipient is required by law or by any regulator to disclose any Confidential Information, it shall give the Company prior written notice and disclose only such part as it is legally required to disclose.

## 4. RESIDUALS

4.1 Notwithstanding anything in this Agreement, the Company shall be free to use Residuals for any purpose, including the development, marketing and procurement of products and services, provided that this Clause 4.1 does not grant any licence under any patent or copyright.

## 5. RETURN OF INFORMATION

## 6. REGULATORY MATTERS

10.2 The Recipient shall indemnify the Company for all losses, costs and expenses (including legal fees) arising from any breach of this Agreement by the Recipient or its Representatives.

## RECITALS

WHEREAS, AtliQ provides data engineering, analytics and AI/ML services to its clients, and requires certain data preparation and annotation services in connection with a client project;

WHEREAS, AtliQ desires to engage Vendor to provide such services, and Vendor desires to provide such services, subject to the terms and conditions of this Agreement;

NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the mutual covenants and agreements set forth herein, the Parties agree as follows:

## ARTICLE 1 — DEFINITIONS

1.1 "**AtliQ Materials**" means all data, datasets, information, systems access, documents and other materials furnished by or on behalf of AtliQ or the End Client.
1.2 "**Deliverables**" means all labelled datasets, annotations, label files, quality reports, documentation and other materials prepared or delivered by or on behalf of Vendor under this Agreement, in whole or in part.
1.3 "**Delivery Date**" means each date for delivery of a Deliverable set forth in the Engagement Schedule.
1.4 "**End Client**" means the client of AtliQ identified in the Engagement Schedule for whose project the Services are performed.
1.5 "**Fees**" means the amounts payable to Vendor as set forth in the Engagement Schedule.
1.6 "**Losses**" means any and all losses, damages, liabilities, deficiencies, claims, actions, judgments, settlements, interest, awards, penalties, fines, costs or expenses of whatever kind, including reasonable legal fees.
1.7 "**Services**" means the services described in Article 2 and in the Engagement Schedule.
1.8 "**Total Fees**" means the aggregate Fees payable under this Agreement as stated in the Engagement Schedule.
1.9 "**Vendor Personnel**" means all partners, employees, agents and contractors of Vendor who perform any portion of the Services.

## ARTICLE 2 — SERVICES

2.1 **Scope.** Vendor shall perform the Services described in the Engagement Schedule.
2.2 **Standards of Performance.** Vendor shall perform the Services in a diligent, professional and workmanlike manner, in accordance with the highest standards of the industry, and in compliance with AtliQ's annotation guidelines and quality requirements made available to Vendor, as updated from time to time.
2.3 **Vendor Personnel.** Vendor shall assign qualified Vendor Personnel. AtliQ may, in its sole discretion, request removal of any Vendor Personnel, and Vendor shall promptly replace such individual at no additional cost to AtliQ.
2.4 **Subcontracting.** Vendor shall not subcontract any portion of the Services without AtliQ's prior written consent. Vendor shall remain fully responsible for any subcontractor's performance.
2.5 **Change Orders.** No change in the scope of Services shall be binding unless set forth in a written change order executed by authorized representatives of both Parties.

## ARTICLE 3 — ACCEPTANCE

3.1 AtliQ shall have fifteen (15) days following delivery of each Deliverable to test and evaluate such Deliverable against the acceptance criteria in the Engagement Schedule, including where AtliQ so elects, review by the End Client.
3.2 If AtliQ determines that a Deliverable does not conform, Vendor shall correct the non-conformity at no cost within five (5) business days. AtliQ may repeat the acceptance process until the Deliverable conforms, or may, at its option, reject the Deliverable and receive a refund of all Fees paid in respect thereof.
3.3 Acceptance shall not be deemed to occur by use, by delivery to the End Client, by payment, or by the passage of time.

## ARTICLE 4 — FEES, INVOICING AND PAYMENT

4.1 **Fees.** AtliQ shall pay Vendor the Fees set forth in the Engagement Schedule. Fees are firm and fixed and shall not be increased during the term of this Agreement.
4.2 **Invoices.** Vendor shall invoice AtliQ monthly in arrears for Deliverables accepted in the preceding month. Each invoice shall be a valid tax invoice under the CGST Act, 2017, state Vendor's GSTIN and PAN, and reference the Agreement No.
4.3 **Payment Terms.** AtliQ's obligation to pay any invoice is conditional upon AtliQ's receipt of payment from the End Client for the corresponding services. AtliQ shall pay each properly submitted, undisputed invoice within fifteen (15) days after AtliQ receives the corresponding payment from the End Client, and in any event not later than one hundred and twenty (120) days after AtliQ's receipt of the invoice.
4.4 **Disputed Amounts.** AtliQ may withhold payment of any amount it disputes in good faith. Vendor shall continue performing the Services during the pendency of any dispute.
4.5 **Set-off.** AtliQ may set off against any amount owed to Vendor any amount owed by Vendor to AtliQ under this Agreement, including liquidated damages.
4.6 **Taxes.** GST shall be payable in addition to the Fees against a valid tax invoice. AtliQ shall deduct tax at source as required under the Income-tax Act, 1961 and furnish the applicable TDS certificate.

## ARTICLE 5 — TERM AND TERMINATION

5.1 **Term.** This Agreement shall commence on the Effective Date and continue until completion of the Services, unless earlier terminated as provided herein.
5.2 **Termination for Cause.** Either Party may terminate this Agreement upon written notice if the other Party materially breaches this Agreement and fails to cure such breach within fifteen (15) days after written notice thereof.
5.3 **Termination for Convenience.** AtliQ may terminate this Agreement, in whole or in part, for any reason or no reason, upon seven (7) days' written notice to Vendor. Upon such termination, AtliQ's sole obligation shall be to pay Fees for Deliverables accepted by AtliQ prior to the effective date of termination; AtliQ shall have no obligation to pay for work in progress, unaccepted Deliverables, demobilization costs or anticipated profits.
5.4 **Effect of Termination.** Upon expiration or termination, Vendor shall immediately deliver to AtliQ all Deliverables, whether complete or incomplete, and return or delete all AtliQ Materials.
5.5 **Survival.** Articles 6, 7, 9, 10, 11 and 12 shall survive expiration or termination.

## ARTICLE 6 — CONFIDENTIALITY

6.1 "**Confidential Information**" means all non-public information disclosed by or on behalf of AtliQ or the End Client, including AtliQ Materials, business plans, technical information and pricing.
6.2 Vendor shall (a) hold Confidential Information in strict confidence, (b) use it only to perform the Services, and (c) disclose it only to those Vendor Personnel with a need to know who are bound by written obligations at least as protective.
6.3 The foregoing obligations shall not apply to information that (a) is or becomes publicly available through no fault of Vendor; (b) was rightfully known without restriction prior to disclosure; (c) is rightfully received from a third party without restriction; or (d) is independently developed without use of Confidential Information.
6.4 Vendor acknowledges that any breach of this Article may cause irreparable harm for which monetary damages would be inadequate, and that AtliQ shall be entitled to injunctive relief.

## ARTICLE 7 — INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY

7.1 **AtliQ Materials.** All AtliQ Materials are and shall remain the sole property of AtliQ or the End Client, as applicable. Nothing in this Agreement grants Vendor any right in AtliQ Materials except the limited right to use them to perform the Services.
7.2 **Vendor IP.** Vendor shall retain all right, title and interest in and to its tools, labelling platform, scripts, ontologies, annotation guidelines developed by Vendor, and annotation outputs, including all intellectual property rights therein (collectively, "**Vendor IP**").
7.3 **Licence to AtliQ.** Subject to payment of the applicable Fees, Vendor grants AtliQ a non-exclusive, non-transferable, perpetual licence to use the annotation outputs and Deliverables for the purposes of the End Client project, including delivery to the End Client.
7.4 **Moral Rights.** To the extent permitted by law, Vendor waives, and shall cause Vendor Personnel to waive, all moral rights in the Deliverables.

## ARTICLE 8 — REPRESENTATIONS AND WARRANTIES

8.1 Each Party represents and warrants that it is duly organized, validly existing and has full power and authority to enter into and perform this Agreement.
8.2 Vendor further represents and warrants that: (a) the Services shall be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; (b) the Deliverables shall meet the accuracy thresholds in the Engagement Schedule; (c) the Deliverables shall not infringe any third-party intellectual property right; and (d) Vendor shall comply with all applicable laws.

## ARTICLE 9 — INDEMNIFICATION

9.1 **By Vendor.** Vendor shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless AtliQ, its Affiliates, and their respective directors, officers, employees, agents, successors and assigns (the "**AtliQ Indemnitees**") from and against any and all Losses arising out of or relating to (a) the Services or Deliverables, (b) any breach of this Agreement by Vendor, (c) any claim by the End Client relating to the Services or Deliverables, or (d) any act or omission of Vendor Personnel, in each case regardless of whether such Losses are caused in whole or in part by the negligence of any AtliQ Indemnitee.
9.2 **Procedure.** AtliQ shall give prompt written notice of any claim. AtliQ shall have the right to participate with counsel of its choice at Vendor's expense. Vendor shall not settle any claim without AtliQ's prior written consent.

## ARTICLE 10 — LIMITATION OF LIABILITY

10.1 **Exclusion of Consequential Damages.** IN NO EVENT SHALL ATLIQ BE LIABLE TO VENDOR FOR ANY INDIRECT, INCIDENTAL, SPECIAL, CONSEQUENTIAL OR PUNITIVE DAMAGES, OR FOR LOST PROFITS, ARISING OUT OF OR RELATING TO THIS AGREEMENT.
10.2 **Cap on AtliQ Liability.** ATLIQ'S AGGREGATE LIABILITY ARISING OUT OF OR RELATING TO THIS AGREEMENT SHALL NOT EXCEED THE FEES ACTUALLY PAID BY ATLIQ TO VENDOR UNDER THIS AGREEMENT.
10.3 **Vendor Liability.** NOTHING IN THIS AGREEMENT SHALL LIMIT OR EXCLUDE VENDOR'S LIABILITY FOR ANY LOSSES, WHETHER DIRECT OR INDIRECT, ARISING OUT OF OR RELATING TO THIS AGREEMENT, INCLUDING VENDOR'S INDEMNIFICATION OBLIGATIONS.

## ARTICLE 11 — DELAY; LIQUIDATED DAMAGES

11.1 **Time of the Essence.** Time is of the essence with respect to each Delivery Date.
11.2 **Liquidated Damages.** If Vendor fails to achieve any Delivery Date, Vendor shall pay AtliQ, as liquidated damages, an amount equal to two percent (2%) of the Total Fees for each calendar day from the Delivery Date until the date the applicable Deliverable is accepted.
11.3 **Cumulative Remedies.** Liquidated damages under this Article are in addition to and not in lieu of AtliQ's right to recover its actual damages, to terminate this Agreement for cause, and to exercise any other right or remedy available at law or in equity. AtliQ may deduct liquidated damages from any amounts otherwise due to Vendor.

## ARTICLE 12 — GOVERNING LAW AND DISPUTE RESOLUTION

12.1 **Governing Law.** This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of India.
12.2 **Escalation.** The Parties shall attempt in good faith to resolve any dispute through escalation to their respective senior management for a period of fifteen (15) days.

title: Karandeep's contract checklist (2024)
text:
# Contract checklist (Karandeep — personal notes)

*(Found in Karandeep's Google Keep; the list itself was last edited March 2024. Shared with Jay once "so you know what I look for". The only written record of how AtliQ reviews contracts.)*

things I check before signing —

- LDs → cap it. never open ended
- liability → 1x fees. NOT unlimited
- indemnity → mutual. we don't cover their mistakes
- payment → 30 days, 45 max
- gov law → ours (India for Pvt Ltd, US for Inc)
- IP → client owns what we build for them, we keep our own stuff
- termination → they pay for work done
- confidentiality → mutual, fine usually
- NDAs → just sign if mutual

check SOW matches proposal (scope, milestones, rates)

---

*Internal note (Karandeep, September 2026, added after the 22 Sep contract-queue meeting):*

*This list is two years old and was never complete. It says nothing about the things that actually worry me now — what we've already promised other clients. Non-competes, exclusivity, pricing promises, who owns what we reused. None of that is in the contract in front of me; it's in contracts I signed a year or three ago and don't remember clause by clause. I review everything myself, usually after 10 pm, and the only "system" is my memory of how the last negotiation went. When I'm rushed I sign things I would never have agreed to on a normal day — Brightwater proved that. We are doing nine contracts a month now. This doesn't scale and it isn't safe.*

*And the list only covers one side of the table. Half of what I sign now isn't a client contract at all — NDAs, partnership agreements with platform companies, and our own agreements with agencies and freelancers we bring in. When we're the buyer, the same clause I'd reject from a client is sitting in our own template. I'd rather sign a mutual NDA than a one-sided one, and I'd rather a deal work for both sides than win it at the other side's expense — a six-person agency or a freelancer shouldn't get our paper and feel the way I felt reading Brightwater's. Nothing written down says any of that either.*

- Signed 28 Apr 2025. He worked on the Acme dashboards.

**Acme Retail (India) — MSA, Mar 2025**
- Their delay clause: LD 1% of Contract Value per week, no cap.
- K countered: 0.5% of the affected milestone fee per week of delay attributable to us, max 5% of that milestone fee, no LD for delays caused by client. "Open-ended isn't something we can sign."
- Accepted. Signed 10 Mar 2025. Indian law, Mumbai arbitration.

**Al Noor Hospitality (Dubai) — MSA, Mar 2025 — Pvt Ltd**
- Non-compete: they asked worldwide, 3 years. K: "Worldwide for three years would stop us working in hospitality altogether." Landed on GCC, term + 18 months.
- LD: they asked 1% of total fees per week capped at 10% of total fees; wouldn't go below 10% cap. We got the weekly 1% calculated on the milestone instead of total fees.
- Bhavin: "I say take it. $185k, 14 properties, first Gulf logo. And on §12 — we'll never do another hotel in the Gulf anyway. I approve the 10% as a one-off."
- K: "Approving 10% of total fees as a strategic exception for Al Noor only — not our new standard."
- DIFC law / DIFC courts — accepted ("group standard for all technology vendors").
- Signed 15 Mar 2025.

**Northwind Logistics (UK) — MSA + SOW-1, Jun 2025 — Pvt Ltd**
- Their paper. LD 10% of Contract Value if go-live missed → K countered 0.5%/week of milestone, cap 5% of milestone, client delays excluded. Agreed.
- Asked for Indian law / Mumbai arbitration. Tom: board policy, English law non-negotiable. K: "English law / LCIA — not worth losing the deal over. Rest looks ok, I skimmed the IP and boilerplate."
- SOW-1 uses PipeKit. Signed 20 Jun 2025.

**CloudSpan (Singapore) — partnership agreement, Aug 2025 — Pvt Ltd**
- Their exclusivity: we (and Affiliates) can't partner with any "Competing Platform" in India, the GCC or Europe.
- K: "We can't do Europe — Europe is where we're growing." Asked for mutual 90-day termination for convenience.
- Agreed: India + GCC only, mutual 90 days. 12% referral fee, co-marketing, 4 certified engineers (Pranav confirmed). Singapore law / SIAC ok.
- Signed 1 Sep 2025.

**CareBridge Clinics (US healthcare) — NDA + MSA + BAA, Aug–Oct 2025 — AtliQ Inc**
- BAA sent to Calloway Stern (Diane Foster) for review — $3,800.
- K asked Pranav to set up an intercompany BAA (AtliQ Inc ↔ Pvt Ltd) so Pune can work on de-identified data. Diane: could be per engagement or a master. K: "Per engagement, keep it simple."
- NDA signed 11 Aug 2025; MSA and BAAs signed 6 Oct 2025. Only de-identified data offshore.

**PixelCraft Studio (design agency, 6 people) — our vendor agreement, Oct 2025**
- Ishaan pushed back on three clauses in our template: 1% per day delay penalty, 60-day payment, unlimited vendor liability.
- K: "He's right. They're six people. I don't want our paper to be the thing I hate receiving." Deleted the penalty, 30-day payment, liability capped at fees for both sides.
- Signed 20 Oct 2025. (Changes made in PixelCraft's copy only — not sure the template file was ever updated.)

**Brightwater Insurance (US) — Services Agreement, Nov 2025 — AtliQ Inc**
- Their group template (UK parent). Mark needed it by 28 Nov (quarter end). Dhaval checked scope only.
- K replied from phone: "Looks standard, signing now."
- No redlines. Signed 28 Nov 2025. *(See April post-mortem.)*

**Kessler Mobility (Germany) — framework agreement, Jan 2026 — didn't sign**
- Their final position: supplier liable "without limitation for all damages".
- Bhavin: "It's ~€120k. Any way we can live with it?" K: "No. Unlimited liability on a €120k deal means one bad incident … and the company is gone." Offered 1x fees with carve-outs.
- No reply. Lost.

**Al Noor — consent letter, Feb 2026**
- K asked Omar for consent under §12 for one project: Seaside Hotels, Muscat (demand forecasting). Letter received 10 Feb. *(Couldn't find where the letter is saved — K has it?)*

**GlobalMart (India) — NDA, Mar 2026**
- They sent a one-way NDA (only us bound). K: "We only sign mutual — we'll be sharing our architecture too." They agreed. Mutual NDA signed 12 Mar 2026.

**Meridian Healthcare (India) — NDA, Jul 2026**
- Bhavin: needed signing that night before a data walkthrough, "it's standard". K signed within the hour. No changes asked.

**Trustline NBFC (India) — MSA, Jul–Aug 2026**
- Their terms: payment 90 days; LD 2% of Contract Value per week, cap 10% of total.
- K: 45 days; 0.5% of milestone fee per week, cap 5% of milestone, client delays excluded. Agreed. Signed 15 Aug 2026.

**Harrington Health (US) — NDA, Aug 2026 — AtliQ Inc**
- Dhaval needed it signed so scoping could start. K signed next day (20 Aug). Nothing discussed.

---

*Jay's note: didn't get to Sunrise, DataNest, Orbit, Seaside or the older NDAs. A lot of the "why" is only in K's head.*

7.2 No liquidated damages shall be payable for delays caused by the Client, including delayed data access, or by Force Majeure.

## 1. DEFINITIONS

1.1 Capitalized terms not defined here have the meanings given in HIPAA, including "Protected Health Information" or "**PHI**", "Limited Data Set", "Breach", "Security Incident" and "Subcontractor".

## 2. PERMITTED USES AND DISCLOSURES

2.1 Business Associate may use and disclose PHI only as necessary to perform the services under the Services Agreement, or as required by law.

2.2 Business Associate shall not de-identify PHI for any purpose other than performing the services, and shall not use de-identified data for its own purposes or for other clients.

## 3. SAFEGUARDS

3.1 Business Associate shall implement administrative, physical and technical safeguards that comply with Subpart C of 45 C.F.R. Part 164.

3.2 Business Associate shall encrypt PHI at rest and in transit using industry-standard encryption.

## 4. SUBCONTRACTORS AND LOCATION OF PROCESSING

4.1 Business Associate shall not engage any Subcontractor that creates, receives, maintains or transmits PHI without Covered Entity's prior written approval.

4.2 Business Associate shall ensure that each approved Subcontractor agrees in writing, before any access, to the same restrictions and conditions that apply to Business Associate under this BAA. **Affiliates of Business Associate are Subcontractors for this purpose.**

4.3 **Offshore restriction.** Business Associate shall not, and shall ensure that its Subcontractors and Affiliates do not, access, store, process, transmit or view PHI — **including any Limited Data Set** — from any location outside the United States, whether directly or through remote access, virtual desktop or screen-sharing.

4.4 Data that has been de-identified in accordance with the Safe Harbor method at 45 C.F.R. §164.514(b)(2) may be accessed outside the United States only with Covered Entity's prior written approval for each data set.

## 5. REPORTING

5.1 Business Associate shall report to Covered Entity any use or disclosure of PHI not permitted by this BAA, any Security Incident, and any Breach of Unsecured PHI without unreasonable delay and in any event within **five (5) business days** of discovery.

5.2 Business Associate shall reimburse Covered Entity's reasonable costs of breach notification, credit monitoring and regulatory response to the extent caused by Business Associate or its Subcontractors.

6.1 Business Associate shall make PHI available for access, amendment and accounting of disclosures as required by 45 C.F.R. §§164.524, 164.526 and 164.528, within ten (10) business days of request.

## 7. TERM AND TERMINATION

7.1 This BAA is coterminous with the Services Agreement (initial term two (2) years, ending August 24, 2027), and continues for as long as Business Associate or any Subcontractor holds PHI.

7.2 Covered Entity may terminate the Services Agreement immediately if Business Associate materially breaches this BAA and does not cure within ten (10) days.

7.3 On termination, Business Associate shall return or destroy all PHI and certify destruction in writing.

## 8. INSURANCE

8.1 Business Associate shall maintain cyber liability insurance with limits of not less than **USD 3,000,000** per claim, naming Covered Entity as additional insured, and provide a certificate on request.

## 9. INDEMNIFICATION

9.1 Business Associate shall indemnify Covered Entity against losses, fines and penalties arising from Business Associate's or its Subcontractors' breach of this BAA. This indemnity is not subject to any limitation of liability in the Services Agreement.

## 10. MISCELLANEOUS

4.1 AtliQ will deliver with a Pune team of four, supplemented by Kriti Data Labs Pvt Ltd (Bengaluru, India), AtliQ's subcontractor, for model development (two data scientists).

4.2 Audience activation will use SyncRiver (SyncRiver Inc, Austin, Texas, USA), a reverse-ETL SaaS tool that copies segment tables into SyncRiver's US-hosted processing environment before pushing them to retail-media platforms.

## 5. Fees

5.1 Time-and-materials, estimated 1,050 hours. Rates for this SOW:

| Role | Hourly rate (EUR) |
| --- | --- |
| Senior Data Engineer | 80 |
| Data Engineer | 63 |
| Data Scientist | 84 |

5.2 Estimated total: EUR 74,000 (approx. USD 87,000). Invoiced monthly; payable within thirty (30) days.

(Bhavin's comment in margin: "rates +8% vs SOW-1 – inflation, should be fine")

## 6. Governing Terms

6.1 This SOW is governed by the MSA. In case of conflict, this SOW prevails for the purposes of this SOW only.

# MASTER SERVICES AGREEMENT

This Master Services Agreement (the "Agreement") is entered into as of ______________, 2026 (the "Effective Date") between Greystone Claims Solutions, Inc., a Delaware corporation with offices at 100 Pearl Street, 12th Floor, Hartford, Connecticut 06103 ("Greystone"), and AtliQ Inc, a Delaware corporation with offices at 101 College Road East, Suite 210, Princeton, New Jersey 08540 ("Provider").

## 1. BACKGROUND

1.1 Greystone is a third-party claims administrator handling personal auto and property claims on behalf of eleven U.S. property and casualty insurers.

1.2 Greystone wishes to engage Provider to build a claims-triage and fraud-indicator analytics platform for use in its own claims operations.

## 2. SERVICES

2.1 SOW-1 covers: (a) ingestion of first-notice-of-loss, adjuster notes and payment data from Greystone's Guidewire ClaimCenter instance; (b) a claims-complexity and fraud-indicator scoring model; and (c) adjuster workload dashboards.

2.2 Provider may use personnel in India for development, provided that claimant personal information is accessed only via Greystone's U.S.-hosted virtual desktop environment and is not downloaded.

## 3. FEES AND PAYMENT

3.1 SOW-1 fees: USD 86,000, payable by milestone (Exhibit A).

3.2 Payment within thirty (30) days of invoice.

## 4. TERM AND TERMINATION

4.1 Two (2) year term. Either party may terminate for uncured material breach (30 days). Greystone may terminate an SOW for convenience on thirty (30) days' notice, paying for work performed and non-cancellable commitments.

## 5. CONFIDENTIALITY

5.1 Mutual. Each party protects the other's Confidential Information with reasonable care; obligations survive three (3) years, and indefinitely for trade secrets and claimant personal information.

## 6. INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY

6.1 Greystone owns Deliverables created specifically for it on payment. Provider retains its pre-existing tools and know-how, and grants Greystone a perpetual, non-exclusive, royalty-free licence to use those incorporated in Deliverables for internal purposes.

## 7. WARRANTIES

7.1 Professional and workmanlike services; Deliverables conform to the SOW for ninety (90) days after acceptance.

## 8. INDEMNIFICATION

8.1 Each party shall indemnify the other against third-party claims to the extent caused by its breach of confidentiality, infringement of intellectual property, or gross negligence or willful misconduct.

## 9. LIMITATION OF LIABILITY

9.1 Neither party is liable for indirect, consequential or punitive damages.

9.2 Each party's aggregate liability is capped at the fees paid or payable under the applicable SOW in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim, except for indemnification obligations and breach of Section 5.

## 10. DELAY

10.1 Liquidated damages of 0.5% of the affected milestone fee per week of Provider-caused delay, capped at 5% of that milestone fee; not applicable to delays caused by Greystone or force majeure.

## 11. DATA SECURITY

11.1 Provider shall comply with the Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act Safeguards Rule as applicable to service providers and with Greystone's security schedule; notify security incidents within seventy-two (72) hours.

## 12. GENERAL

12.1 Governing law. Laws of the State of Delaware. Exclusive venue: state and federal courts in Wilmington, Delaware.

12.2 Insurance. Provider shall maintain professional liability and cyber liability insurance of $1,000,000 each.

12.3 Non-solicitation. Mutual, twelve (12) months, employees engaged in the Services.

12.4 Assignment. Neither party may assign without consent, except to a successor by merger.
